QualityLayer
The software factory with you in the loop

**Plan, implement and verify software with your favorite coding agents.**
Work side by side in the App or browser, or in your own agent: terminal, IDE or agent app.

Install • Workflow • Docs • Website • Changelog • Issues

Download the App  

  Watch the [full-resolution video](https://qualitylayer-media.max-ritter.workers.dev/hero-walkthrough-v2026111301.mp4) or [try the demo](https://qualitylayer.dev/app-demo/?story&guide) in your browser. Fictional project.
--- ## Why QualityLayer > “With QualityLayer, developing software with agents finally feels like doing real engineering again.” > > *An engineer who uses QualityLayer* | You get | How it works | | --- | --- | | **Your own agent and plan** | Use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more with your existing login or API key. | | **A design you can review** | Ask your agent about diagrams and clickable screens, then approve the Plan before code changes. | | **Small, tested changes** | Your agent writes tests before code and hands independent parts to other agents when useful. | | **An independent check** | With independent review on, a separate agent checks the running change against your request before you review it. | | **Your own requirements** | Add checks, tools or skills to any step. Your agent records what ran, what did not, and why. [Step checks](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/reference/settings#step-checks). | | **Your own automations** | Send task events to a URL or a command, and read or start tasks from a script. [Automations](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/automations). | | **Visible decisions and effort** | Read decisions and results in your repository; see time, model usage value and cost estimates in the App. | ---

Getting started

### Prerequisites - **A coding agent**, installed and signed in with your subscription or API key: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Antigravity, Pi, OpenCode or GitHub Copilot. [Other agents](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/agents/other) connect through the CLI. - **Git** and a repository. ### Installation **[Download the App](https://qualitylayer.dev/download)** and open it. Setup automatically installs the `qualitylayer` command ([commands](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/reference/commands)) and connects your agents. On a server, in WSL or in a container: ```bash curl -fsSL https://qualitylayer.dev/install.sh | bash # macOS, Linux, WSL irm https://qualitylayer.dev/install.ps1 | iex # Windows PowerShell ``` The App updates itself; without it, run `qualitylayer update`. To work on a Linux or macOS machine you reach over ssh, add it under **Settings › Machines**: the App installs QualityLayer there and lets you set up its agents and projects. [Installation guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/install).
Uninstalling `qualitylayer uninstall` undoes what the installer changed; your plans stay. On Windows, even when the App is gone: ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://qualitylayer.dev/install.ps1))) -Uninstall ```
Coming from Pilot Shell 11 Run `pilot update` or download the App. An active Pilot Shell licence works with both products; older purchases may need help moving over. [Migration and memory import](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/moving-from-pilot-shell).
### First steps In the App or browser, choose **+**, then **Task** (Feature or Bugfix) or **Chat**. Pick your repository and agent, and describe what you need: ```text Plan retries for failed webhooks and stop after a few tries. ``` 1. Answer questions and ask your agent to revise the Plan. 2. Approve the Plan. Your agent builds and verifies the change. 3. Review the result and recorded checks, then approve it. Ask your agent to merge, deploy or make further changes. Prefer your terminal, IDE or agent app? Choose **In my own agent**, or ask there: “Using QualityLayer, plan retries for failed webhooks.” Other agents use the CLI ([supported agents](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/agents/native)). **Chat** skips the workflow steps ([Chat guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/chat)). QualityLayer runs only when you ask for it. [Your first task](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/first-task). ### Skills your agent gets Setup adds these skills. Ask in plain words, in any language. | Skill | For | You say | | --- | --- | --- | | `ql-peer` | Agents talking to each other | “Ask Codex to review what you just built.” | | `ql-workflow` | Plan, implement and verify a change | “Using QualityLayer, add rate limits to the export API.” | | `ql-chat` | Chat without workflow steps | “Using QualityLayer, chat about the billing refactor.” | | `ql-artifact` | Designs, diagrams and pages | “Open the settings design in my browser.” | | `ql-quality` | Code health and security scans | “Scan this repository for leaked secrets.” | | `ql-manage` | Tasks, settings and setup | “Show my open tasks.” | [More about the skills](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/agents/native#the-six-skills) ---

The workflow

Three steps, two approvals. You plan and you verify; agents do everything between. Each step is one page in the App and one Markdown file in your repository, and existing plans start at Plan. ### 1 · Plan, approved by you Your agent reads the code, asks what only you can answer and writes one Plan: **Done means**, named diagrams and clickable screens. Compare revisions after feedback. Bugs are reproduced and diagnosed here. [Plan guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/steps/plan) ### 2 · Implement, by your agents Your agent cuts the Plan into slices and task cards, writes a failing test before each change and hands independent slices to other agents. Follow progress on the slice board or dependency graph, and open any finished slice's diff. By default it commits after each checked slice; you can choose one commit before Verify or review the checked worktree diff first. [Implement guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/steps/implement) ### 3 · Verify, then approved by you Agents that did not write the code check every point and fix what fails. Then the same page is your review: an ordered stack of slices, a slice dependency graph, built screens and each point as it ran. [Verify guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/steps/verify) **Then the pull request.** Your agent fixes failing checks and routine review threads; the task stays open until you merge. [Pull request guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/steps/pull-request) ## Checks and independent review Your project's checks, [code health](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/reference/code-health) and security scans run first. Then a separate agent reviews the change against your request. [How Verify works](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/steps/verify). ## QualityLayer App | In the App | What you can do | | --- | --- | | **Chat or a planned task** | Talk directly with your agent or follow the workflow. See agent activity and get notified when one needs you. | | **Conversation and terminal** | Read the agent's conversation or its terminal beside the task. Answer questions and send quick feedback on marked text, code or artifact spots. | | **Artifacts** | Try clickable designs, keep them in your repository, and export designs, Plans and Reviews for teammates. [Artifacts guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/artifacts). | | **Checks and code review** | Read the evidence, review diffs slice by slice or since the last check round, and ask your agent about any line. | | **Agent controls and usage** | Switch agents, choose model, effort and permissions; track limits and daily costs, including in the macOS menu bar. [Settings](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/reference/settings). | | **Local memory** | Reuse [project lessons](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/memory), with optional project Git export and explicit repository import. | QualityLayer keeps tasks, Chats, artifacts and memories on machines you control. Your coding agent uses its own provider. [Files and privacy](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/reference/files#privacy). [Read about the App](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/app) ---
**Quality by design.** The software factory with you in the loop. Made by [Max Ritter](https://maxritter.net) · [License](LICENSE)

import { Card, CardGroup, Steps, Step, Tabs, Tab, Tip, Note, Warning, Screenshot, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

Eight coding agents run natively: QualityLayer adds its skills and hooks to each, and the App shows their sessions. Each keeps its own login and provider.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Install your agent">Sign in and start it once from a terminal.</Step>
  <Step title="Run Setup">The App's Setup, or `qualitylayer agents check`, connects every supported agent it finds. If Codex asks you to review hooks, review and allow only QualityLayer's entries before using Conversation.</Step>
  <Step title="Start a task">**+ › Task** in the App, or tell your agent "Using QualityLayer, plan a CSV export" (**QL** works too, in any language).</Step>
</Steps>

<Screenshot name="new-task" alt="New task in the App: the planner shows agent, model and effort in one row" />

| Agent | Checked with | What QualityLayer adds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup) | 2.1.306 | Skills, lifecycle hooks and its existing prompt integration |
| [Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) | 0.167.1 (macOS) | Skills, implicit invocation policies and lifecycle hooks |
| [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/installation) | 2026.10.19 | Skills and lifecycle hooks in its own hooks file |
| [Grok](https://docs.x.ai/build/overview) | 1.0.62 | Skills and hooks, in its own hooks folder |
| [Antigravity](https://antigravity.google/docs/getting-started/) | 1.4.12 | Skills, a workflow command and lifecycle hooks |
| [Pi](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/quickstart) | 1.2.0 | Skills, a lifecycle extension and fresh helper sessions |
| [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai/docs/) | 2.0.29 | Skills, a command and a lifecycle plugin |
| [GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli) | 1.0.105 | Skills, a hook file and the memory server |

<Note>Cursor, Grok and Antigravity are set up only after you have started them once from a terminal. GitHub Copilot Business and Enterprise need an organization admin to enable Copilot CLI in the Copilot policies.</Note>

## The six skills {#the-six-skills}

Ask in plain words; your agent picks the skill. An ordinary coding request does not start a workflow.

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="ql-workflow" icon="network" tone="plan" href="/docs/steps/plan">Plan, build, verify and review a change. The only skill that starts a task.</Card>
  <Card title="ql-artifact" icon="shapes" href="/docs/artifacts">Mockups, diagrams and clickable pages.</Card>
  <Card title="ql-manage" icon="list-todo" href="/docs/memory">Tasks, memory, settings and setup.</Card>
  <Card title="ql-peer" icon="messages-square" href="/docs/reference/commands#session-messaging">Sessions of any of these agents review each other or hand over a task.</Card>
  <Card title="ql-quality" icon="badge-check" href="/docs/reference/code-health">Code complexity, structure and duplication.</Card>
  <Card title="ql-chat" icon="message-square" href="/docs/chat">A Chat without workflow steps.</Card>
</CardGroup>

## Models and reviews

Pick the agent, model and effort for each task. High is the default. OpenCode models without effort levels use their own defaults.

| Agent | Model choices |
| --- | --- |
| Codex | The models your Codex account offers, as Codex lists them; a default your plan lacks moves to Codex's own model |
| Pi / OpenCode | Provider-qualified IDs: `openai-codex/gpt-6.1-sol` / `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`; both can use a Copilot subscription |
| Cursor / Antigravity | Effort is part of the model name, such as Opus 5.5 (High) |
| GitHub Copilot | Auto works on every plan; paid plans can choose Claude Opus 5.5 |

Codex, OpenCode and Cursor model menus follow the models their native clients report. A selected model missing from that list stays visible with **· not offered**. When Antigravity reports models, its menus show their names and launch each selection with its exact model ID. The remaining menus include the models QualityLayer knows. For a custom Antigravity model, choose **Add a model…** and enter the configured ID you pass to `agy --model`. OpenCode’s Ollama provider gets up to 15 minutes to send response headers by default, in the App and in your terminal. Set `providers.ollama.settings.headerTimeout` in OpenCode to override the default for that provider.

Reviewers work in a separate context and edit nothing. Cursor and Antigravity review disposable copies and stop at the first tool that is not read-only ([choosing reviewers](../reference/settings.mdx#second-opinion)).

## Sessions in the App

The **Conversation** view reads each agent's session record ([controls](../app.mdx#agent-runs)). Some records hold less:

| Agent | What its Conversation lacks |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode | Nothing |
| Grok | Context fill, permission questions |
| Antigravity | Permission questions |
| Cursor | Thinking, tool output, token counts, context fill, permission questions |
| GitHub Copilot | Permission questions |

Permission waits show in Conversation. A reply that only the Terminal view shows gets **Open Terminal**. Cursor gets numbered workflow questions; the others ask in their own picker ([In your agent](../work-in-your-agent.mdx#pickers)).

After a crash, stop the old run and ask "Using QL, continue verification of task retry-webhooks."

### Permission modes {#permission-modes}

New managed sessions start in Bypass unless you saved a global or per-agent mode; **Agent settings** keeps the agent's own policy. A new task opens with the agent and choices you last planned with, and a build with those you last built with. A build on the planning agent keeps the planning session's choices, including permission changes you accepted.

| Agent | Modes |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code | Auto, Ask first, Accept edits, Bypass |
| Codex | On request, Ask first, Auto review, Full access |
| Cursor | Ask first, Auto-review, Run everything |
| Grok | Auto, Ask first, Accept edits, Bypass |
| Antigravity | Ask first, Auto, Accept edits, Bypass |
| OpenCode | Agent settings, Auto-approve |
| Pi | None; its own tool permissions apply |
| GitHub Copilot | Manual Approval, Assisted Permissions, Allow All; older sessions use the Terminal view's `/permissions` menu |

<Warning>Switching a running session to Bypass, Full access or Run everything asks you to confirm. **Apply and continue** changes permissions at a supported prompt and resumes the conversation. Pi has no bypass switch, and OpenCode keeps explicit denials. Your Plan and final approvals stay separate.</Warning>


### Plan limits {#plan-limits}

**Claude Code**, **Codex** and **GitHub Copilot** show the usage windows their records report, such as **Week · 58 % used**; [Usage display](../reference/settings.mdx#usage) switches the App and the macOS menu bar to **Remaining**. Missing or reset readings stay unknown. Agents billed by use show the session's estimated cost instead.

When one of them stops at its limit, the task shows **Limit · resets 17:23**. With **Resume when a limit resets** on, QualityLayer continues the session then; **Cancel resume** stops that. Otherwise copy the command that continues it.

## How QualityLayer finds your agents {#finding-agents}

**Not installed** means it was not found. Enter the full path in **⋯ › Edit launch…** › **Command**, such as `/opt/tools/bin/codex`, or press **Check again**.

<details>
<summary>Search order</summary>

1. The **Command** you set. If it cannot run, the agent counts as missing.
2. The App's PATH, then your login shell's PATH.
3. `~/.local/bin`, `~/.codex/packages/standalone/current/bin`, Homebrew, `~/.npm-global/bin`, Bun, Volta, pnpm, nvm and fnm.
4. npm's global folder.
5. For Codex, the command inside the ChatGPT or Codex desktop app.

`--version` must name the agent, such as `codex-cli 0.163.0`.

</details>

## Setup and removal

`qualitylayer agents list` and `qualitylayer agents check` match **Settings › Agents**. Pi's files go to `~/.pi/agent`, OpenCode's to `~/.config/opencode`, GitHub Copilot's to `~/.copilot`. Updates replace only unchanged files QualityLayer owns; uninstall keeps your logins, settings, session history and edited files.

  { title: "Other agents", href: "/docs/agents/other", text: "Any agent that runs shell commands, through the CLI." },
  { title: "In your agent", href: "/docs/work-in-your-agent", text: "Answer and approve in your agent's chat." },
  { title: "Settings", href: "/docs/reference/settings#second-opinion", text: "Second opinion and reviewers." },

---
title: The App
description: Read the work, answer questions and work beside your agent’s conversation.

import { Card, CardGroup, Steps, Step, Tabs, Tab, Tip, Note, Screenshot, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

Read the task on the left and work with your agent on the right. Use the desktop App on macOS, Windows or Linux, or run `qualitylayer app` for the same workspace in your browser.

<Screenshot name="home" alt="Home: the sidebar with projects, tasks and plan limits, beside a Needs you section for your questions and approvals and a separate Running section for your agents' work" caption="Example projects and people are fictional." />

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="Sidebar" icon="list-todo" href="#sidebar">Search, Home, Artifacts and your tasks and Chats by project. **+** starts a **Task** or a [Chat](chat.mdx).</Card>
  <Card title="Step page" icon="network" href="/docs/steps/plan">Where the task stands, and its result. A person icon marks the two steps you approve.</Card>
  <Card title="Right sidebar" icon="message-square" href="#agent-runs">**Conversation**, **Terminal** and **Files**, beside the page.</Card>
</CardGroup>

The **Agent status** chip in the top bar says whether your agent is working, needs you, is quiet or has stopped.

## The sidebar {#sidebar}

Projects group tasks by repository, with tasks waiting on you first. A row shows the step strip, coloured by stage, and live agent activity; amber means it needs you. Its toggle opens the task lists Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode report, and their helpers.

- Right-click a project to rename, recolor or hide it; right-click a task to rename, archive or delete it.
- The foot shows [plan limits](agents/native.mdx#plan-limits) or today's cost. With [machines](machines.mdx), the head switches computers.
- **View options** filters names, groups and row sizes. **Last activity** keeps tasks changed in the last 24 h, 3 d or 7 d; working and open tasks stay visible.
- Drag past the narrowest width to collapse the sidebar into a rail of Home, Artifacts, waiting and running tasks, plan limits and Settings. Pull the rail outward to reopen it.

**⌘K** searches actions, projects, tasks and files; **⌘P** opens a file in the current task. Use Ctrl instead of ⌘ on Windows and Linux.

<details>
<summary>More shortcuts in the installed App</summary>

| Shortcut | Action |
| --- | --- |
| **⇧⌘N** | New task |
| **⌘B** / **⌘J** | Toggle the left / right sidebar |
| **⌘1** / **⌘2** | Home / Artifacts |
| **⌘,** | Settings |

A focused Terminal keeps the agent's keys, including **Ctrl+Enter** for Claude Code's send now.

</details>

## Home {#home}

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="Needs you" icon="message-square" tone="plan">Questions, approvals, waiting Chats and agents that stopped early.</Card>
  <Card title="Running" icon="code-xml" tone="implement">Active work, ten rows at a time.</Card>
  <Card title="Shipped lately" icon="git-pull-request" tone="verify">Your three newest shipped tasks.</Card>
</CardGroup>

When nothing waits or runs, one **All clear** line offers **New task**. A request you typed into New task and closed waits on Home with **Continue**. Notifications arrive when you can act: an agent needs you, it is your turn, or a run stopped early.

## Answering questions {#questions}

<Screenshot name="question" alt="A Plan question in Your turn: the recommended choice open with its diagram, the other folded to one line, and your own answer below" />

**Your turn** shows one question; its numbered strip lets you answer in any order. Where choices have facts, the recommended one is open and the others fold to one line. A question about a screen shows that screen in the card. Answers are saved immediately and never approve the Plan or the change. If you pause or stop the agent, it resumes only when you choose.

<details>
<summary>Answer with the keyboard</summary>

| Key | Action |
| --- | --- |
| **1–9** | Pick a choice |
| **R** / **A** | Take this recommendation / all recommendations in the batch |
| **T** | Write your own answer, then **Send** |
| **M** | **Tell me more** |
| **Enter** | Take the recommendation when the card is focused |

</details>

## Documents and your agent {#comments-and-artifacts}

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Files" icon="file-text">Every document, artifact, review and record, plus **Review the code** and **View changes**. **Records** opens `records/`, `evidence/` and `agents/`.</Card>
  <Card title="Reader" icon="app-window">A whole document, with **On this page** and **Copy document**. Step documents end with **For agents**.</Card>
</CardGroup>

**Copy as Markdown** keeps Mermaid and local picture names; **Copy formatted** includes PNG pictures. Working artifacts are compact entries in **Files**; **Open full size** opens the whole page.

Select a passage or mark code lines to leave quick feedback. For an artifact, choose **Feedback**, then mark a spot or area. Write your remark, add files or paste an image, then send it to your agent’s Conversation or Terminal. A request never approves a Plan, changes approved scope or settles the final approval.

## Code review {#code-review}

<Screenshot name="verify-review" alt="The code review: the changed files by slice beside the diff, with why each file changed" />

Open **Changes** in the header or **Review the code** in Verify or Files. Choose one file or all files, **Unified / Split** diffs, or **Full file › Version** for an exact revision. **Viewed** records your reading progress; **All viewed** and **Clear** apply to every file. **Exit** returns to where you came from; while your approval waits it reads **Finish code review**.

## What it costs {#cost}

**Cost** in the task header estimates each step from local logs at verified API prices; for Copilot it shows its recorded AI-credit value, which is not money billed on top. Unknown values show a dash. Amounts stay hidden until you open it. **Usage history** opens **Settings › Usage**.

## Agent runs {#agent-runs}

When you start a task or the build, choose where the agent runs:

<Tabs groupId="where">
  <Tab value="app" label="In the App">Recommended. Pick the agent, model, effort and branch. You answer in **Conversation**.</Tab>
  <Tab value="agent" label="In my own agent">Your terminal, IDE or agent app. Ask it in your own words, or copy the prepared prompt. It asks in its own chat; you can still approve a ready Plan and the finished change in the App.</Tab>
</Tabs>

Closing the sidebar keeps the run. The agent’s menu has **Interrupt** (**Esc**), **Stop session** and **Move to my own agent…**; **Resume** returns. **Continue in another agent…** lets you choose a new agent, model and effort for this task. The previous conversation stays available in history.

**Conversation** folds finished turns to one line; **Terminal** shows the agent's own program. Below the message box sit activity, model, effort, [permissions](agents/native.mdx#permission-modes), pacing and context; each opens its own details. Paste or drop files in either view.

<Tip>**Messages while working** steers your agent at its next step where it supports that, and otherwise queues without interrupting. Choose **Queue until the turn ends** to wait instead. Thinking can be hidden, collapsed or expanded under **Agent controls › Appearance…**.</Tip>

## Stop, archive or delete a task {#stop-archive-or-delete-a-task}

| | How | What stays |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Stop** | Tell your agent | The documents |
| **Archive** | The task header (**More** on compact screens); **Restore** undoes it | Everything |
| **Delete** | Confirm **Delete** in the task header | Task documents and local records are removed; the code and branch stay |

A task from the earlier seven-step workflow cannot be continued or approved. It stays in the task list marked **earlier workflow**, and **Files** opens its documents.

## In Claude Code {#in-claude-code}

The band above your prompt shows only the task attached to that Claude Code session. An ordinary session stays quiet; `/task-pane` adds the steps, build progress and every task that needs you, runs or has an open pull request.

---
title: Artifacts
description: Create and review mockups, diagrams and clickable pages with your agent, then keep local revisions.
mdx:
  format: mdx
---

import { Card, CardGroup, Steps, Step, Tip, Note, Screenshot, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

An artifact is a mockup, a diagram or a clickable set of pages you work on with your agent. A **draft** belongs to one task; a **lasting artifact** is kept for the project.

<Screenshot name="artifacts-open" alt="An open artifact: a clickable page of the example project, with its pages and view controls" />

## Create and review {#create-and-review}

Ask "Using QL, show two layouts for the settings page." No workflow starts. A task's draft appears as a compact entry in **Files**.

<Tip>With **In my own agent**, **Create and copy** creates the artifact and copies its request; the folder chip copies its path. Paste it into any supported agent, or ask in your own words.</Tip>

### Ask about a spot {#full-size}

On a Plan preview, choose **Annotate** to click elements or drag rectangles across several places—capturing each element's `#id` and bounding box—and send all pinned notes to the planner in one batch. In the full-size viewer, **Feedback** marks a spot, area or selected words. Marking alone sends nothing.

### Preview it {#preview}

Switch **Light**, **Dark**, **Desktop** and **Phone**; **F** goes full screen. Buttons and links work, and pages may run their own scripts, but nothing loads from the network. **Export** saves this page or all pages as PDF, PNG images or a static web page. Your agent checks each page in both themes and widths before you see it.

## The Library {#artifacts-place}

<Screenshot name="artifacts" alt="The Artifacts Library: artifacts by project, with search, filters and favorites" />

**Artifacts** in the sidebar holds the **Library**. Search by project, artifact or page, narrow with **Filters**, and switch between **List** and **Gallery**. Starred **Favorites** sit above the list. The row menu renames, copies, archives or deletes; **Archived › Recently deleted** restores.

<Note>Artifacts and their source stay on machines you control. A copy is independent, and listing an artifact in another local project uploads nothing.</Note>

## Lasting artifacts {#lasting}

### Keep a draft {#keep}

**Save to library…** in a draft's menu stores it **In the repository**, where it travels with commits, or **Only on this computer**, out of Git. To change a lasting artifact, ask your agent to draft on it. **Files** keeps its source, metadata and revisions together. Restoring a revision keeps the artifact's identity; removing a registration never deletes the application source it points to.

### Fold in at Verify {#fold-in}

<Steps>
  <Step title="See what changed">Verify shows **This task changes …**; the original stays until then.</Step>
  <Step title="Pick the pages">**Compare** shows both versions.</Step>
  <Step title="Fold them in">**Fold N pages in**. They join the pull request only with a Git action you authorize.</Step>
</Steps>

## Existing artifacts {#existing-artifacts}

Artifacts from earlier versions keep working. Their old share-link details, notes and attachments stay on your computer as read-only history.

pages.automations.mdx: --- title: Automations description: Send task events to your own tools as signed webhooks or commands, and read or start tasks from a script. mdx: format: mdx --- import { Card, CardGroup, Steps, Step, Note, Screenshot, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit"; Send task events to your own tools as signed webhooks or commands, and read or start tasks from a script. ## Your first webhook in 2 minutes {#your-first-webhook-in-2-minutes} Save this as `receiver.mjs`: ```js title="receiver.mjs" import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto" import { createServer } from "node:http" const secret = process.env.QL_SECRET ?? "" createServer((req, res) => { let body = "" req.on("data", (chunk) => (body += chunk)) req.on("end", () => { const [t, v1] = (req.headers["qualitylayer-signature"] ?? "") .split(",") .map((part) => part.slice(part.indexOf("=") + 1)) const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.${body}`).digest("hex") const ok = v1?.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(v1), Buffer.from(expected)) console.log(ok ? "verified" : "bad signature", JSON.parse(body).event) res.writeHead(ok ? 200 : 401).end() }) }).listen(8787) ``` `qualitylayer automations add --url http://127.0.0.1:8787/hook`. The reply shows the automation's `id` and its signing `secret`. `QL_SECRET= node receiver.mjs`, with that secret. `qualitylayer automations test `. The receiver prints `verified automation.test`. From now on every task event reaches it. In the App, the same steps are **Settings › Automations › Add**, then the send button on its row. Your agent can set it up too: "Send QualityLayer events to https://example.com/hook." ## Manage automations {#manage-automations} | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `automations add --url ` | Send events to a URL as signed JSON | | `automations add --command ""` | Run a command with each event as JSON on its input | | `automations list` | Your automations, with each one's last delivery | | `automations set --off` | Turn one off or on, or change its target, `--events` or `--projects` | | `automations test ` | Send a sample `automation.test` event now and print the result | | `automations log []` | The last deliveries, newest first, and why one failed | | `automations secret ` | A URL's signing secret | | `automations events` | The event names | | `automations remove ` | Remove one and drop what waits for it | Every command takes `--json`. `--events task.shipped,task.merged` sends only some events; `--projects shop` sends only some projects' tasks. Both default to all. ## Events {#events} Every event has the same envelope. `task.step` is `plan`, `implement`, `verify` or `shipped`. ```json { "id": "evt_6f1c0a93d27e4b58", "event": "task.step_changed", "at": "2026-11-11T09:41:07.120Z", "version": 1, "project": { "id": "shop-4f2a91c07b1e", "name": "shop" }, "task": { "id": "shop-4f2a91c07b1e~2026-11-11-csv-export", "slug": "2026-11-11-csv-export", "title": "CSV export", "type": "feature", "step": "implement", "link": "http://127.0.0.1:41888/#/task/shop-4f2a91c07b1e~2026-11-11-csv-export" }, "data": { "from": "plan", "to": "implement" } } ``` | Event | When | `data` | | --- | --- | --- | | `task.created` | A task starts | `{}` | | `task.step_changed` | A task moves to another step | `{"from": "plan", "to": "implement"}` | | `question.asked` | The agent asks you something | `{"count": 1, "questions": ["Which export format?"]}` | | `question.answered` | You answer | `{"question": "Which export format?"}` | | `approval.requested` | The Plan, or the change after Verify's checks, waits for your approval | `{"for": "plan"}` or `{"for": "verify"}` | | `approval.decided` | You approve or ask for changes | `{"for": "verify", "decision": "approved"}`, or `"changes"` | | `task.verified` | Verify's checks pass and the change waits for your review | `{"round": 1}`, the checking round that passed | | `task.shipped` | You approve the finished change | `{"slices": 2}` | | `task.merged` | Its pull request is merged | `{"url": "https://github.com/acme/shop/pull/42", "number": 42}` | | `task.archived` | A task is archived | `{}` | From start to shipped, a task sends these events in order. Question events come whenever the agent asks. ```text task.created approval.requested {"for": "plan"} approval.decided {"for": "plan", "decision": "approved"} task.step_changed {"from": "plan", "to": "implement"} task.step_changed {"from": "implement", "to": "verify"} task.verified {"round": 1} approval.requested {"for": "verify"} approval.decided {"for": "verify", "decision": "approved"} task.step_changed {"from": "verify", "to": "shipped"} task.shipped {"slices": 2} ``` `link` opens the task in the App on the computer that sent the event. A test send has the event `automation.test` and a sample task. ## Signature {#signature} A URL receives a `POST` with these headers: | Header | Value | | --- | --- | | `QualityLayer-Event` | The event's name | | `QualityLayer-Delivery` | The event's `id`, the same on every retry | | `QualityLayer-Signature` | `t=,v1=` | `v1` is the HMAC-SHA256 of `.` with the automation's signing secret, as in the receiver above. `t` is the time of that try, so you can refuse old ones. Compare signatures in constant time, and drop an event whose `id` you already have. ## Delivery and retries {#delivery-and-retries} A 2xx answer within 10 seconds. Redirects are not followed. After 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 6 hours, then given up. Every try sends the same body and `id`. One task's events arrive in order: a later one waits while an earlier one is retried. Other tasks go on. A failing automation never holds a task. **Settings › Automations** and `automations log` show what failed. QualityLayer keeps running in the background until a failed delivery's tries are done, and they go on after sleep or a restart. Events are sent from the computer that runs the task; nothing passes through qualitylayer.dev. An event carries the task's title and, for a question, its text, never your answer. ## Run a command {#run-a-command} ```sh #!/bin/sh # ./scripts/on-event.sh: close the ticket when a task ships event=$(cat) [ "$QUALITYLAYER_EVENT" = "task.shipped" ] || exit 0 ./scripts/close-ticket.sh "$(echo "$event" | jq -r .task.title)" ``` `qualitylayer automations add --command "./scripts/on-event.sh"` runs it once per event, in the task's project folder, with the event's name in `QUALITYLAYER_EVENT`. It has 60 seconds. Exit 0 is delivered; a command is never run twice, and its exit code and last output are kept in the log. ## Read and start tasks from a script {#read-and-start-tasks-from-a-script} | Command | Returns | | --- | --- | | `tasks --json` | The project's tasks with id, title, step and dates | | `status --task --json` | One task's step, progress and what it waits for | | `tasks --cost --since 30d --json` | Each task of the period with its step, cost, active time and tokens | | `task start "" --json` | A new task that waits on Home, with its id | | `task start --from --json` | The same, from a GitHub or GitLab issue or pull request, a Jira issue or a Confluence page | | `task start "" --plan [--agent ]` | The same, and planning starts with your default agent, or the one `--agent` names | | `task start "" --planners codex:gpt-6.2-astra:high` | The same for a feature, with up to two extra planners (`agent:model[:effort]`, comma-separated) that review its Plan instead of the second opinion. Each is an extra paid planning run | Run them in the project's folder. `--plan` starts an agent on your plan with every call. `tasks --cost` answers within 20 seconds; when it says `"complete": false`, run it again for the rest. No event and none of these commands approves a Plan or a finished change, or answers a question.

import { Steps, Step, Tabs, Tab, Tip, Note, Screenshot, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

Pick a small change in a repository you know. You describe it, answer a few questions and approve twice; your agent does the rest.

![Your first task: describe the change, answer the questions, approve the Plan, agents build and check, you review and approve, then merge](pathname:///img/diagrams/firsttask-light.svg)
![Your first task: describe the change, answer the questions, approve the Plan, agents build and check, you review and approve, then merge](pathname:///img/diagrams/firsttask-dark.svg)

## Plan, build and review {#steps}

<Screenshot name="new-task" alt="New task in the App: Feature or Bugfix, the request, where the agent runs, and the planner as agent, model and effort" />

<Steps>
  <Step title="Describe the change">Choose **+ › Task**, then **Feature** or **Bugfix**. Describe the change, attach files if needed, then choose your agent and where it runs.</Step>
  <Step title="Answer the questions">They come one at a time in **Your turn**. Each answer reaches your agent at once.</Step>
  <Step title="Approve the Plan">Read it, then choose **Approve and build here**. To ask for a change, mark the Plan and write quick feedback. **Choose where to build** picks another agent or workspace.</Step>
  <Step title="Let it build">Follow Implement and Verify, or do something else. Anything only you can do reaches you as one question.</Step>
  <Step title="Review and approve">On Verify, **Review the code**, see what changed and how **Done means** ran, then approve.</Step>
  <Step title="Merge">**Pull request** on Verify opens GitHub.com or gives you a draft to copy to your host. Create and merge the request there.</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip>To reuse a plan you already have, choose **Existing plan**, paste or attach it, then **Start from this plan** ([details](steps/plan.mdx#a-bug)). **+ › Chat** starts a conversation without steps ([Chat](chat.mdx)).</Tip>

## Where your agent runs

**New task** and **Start the build** both ask.

<Tabs groupId="where">
  <Tab value="app" label="In the App">Recommended. Pick the agent, model, effort, project and branch. Questions and requests to your agent happen in the App.</Tab>
  <Tab value="agent" label="In my own agent">Ask your agent in your terminal, IDE or agent app in your own words, or copy the prepared prompt; attached files are listed by path. The agent asks in its own chat. You can still approve in the App, or [work only in your agent](work-in-your-agent.mdx).</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Good to know {#good-to-know}

- Say QualityLayer or QL when you ask your agent to start work. Follow-up answers continue the task; no slash command is needed.
- Select a passage, write in the quick feedback field and press **Enter** to send it. **Shift+Enter** starts a new line.
- You can stop or pause the run. Your agent's own permission and sign-in prompts still need you.
- To continue elsewhere, stop the run and ask: "Using QL, continue task retry-webhooks." The Plan and evidence stay with the task.
- With several approved Plans waiting, "Implement this using QualityLayer" lists their commands.

pages.install.mdx: --- title: Install description: Install the QualityLayer App on macOS, Windows or Linux, or the command line on a server, WSL2 or a dev container. mdx: format: mdx --- import { Card, CardGroup, Steps, Step, Tabs, Tab, Note, Warning, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit"; Install the App on a computer with a screen. On WSL2, a dev container or a server, install the command line and open the App in your browser. ![One rule: a machine with a screen gets the App, which updates itself; WSL2, dev containers and servers get the command line and open the App in a browser](pathname:///img/diagrams/install-light.svg) ![One rule: a machine with a screen gets the App, which updates itself; WSL2, dev containers and servers get the command line and open the App in a browser](pathname:///img/diagrams/install-dark.svg) ## What you need macOS, Windows or Linux, with Git. Any Git repository you work in. A [supported](agents/native.mdx) or [other](agents/other.mdx) agent, signed in and started once. ## On your computer **[Download the App](https://qualitylayer.dev/download)** and open it. **[Download the App](https://qualitylayer.dev/download)**, or install the App and the command line from PowerShell: ```powershell irm https://qualitylayer.dev/install.ps1 | iex ``` Setup activates your licence or 7-day trial, installs the `qualitylayer` command and connects your agents and recent repositories. ## Agent setup {#agent-setup} Setup adds missing Claude Code, Codex and Grok settings, such as native task tools, commits without attribution and questions that wait for you ([full list](reference/settings.mdx#what-setup-sets)). Settings you chose stay. If you have not chosen native permissions, Claude Code starts in **Bypass** and Codex in **Full access**, also outside QualityLayer. Choose another mode in **Settings › Agents › Edit launch…** or in the agent itself. ## Without the desktop App {#browser} `qualitylayer app` opens the same workspace in your browser. Agents run where QualityLayer is installed. ### WSL2, dev containers and servers {#without-a-screen} ![Install QualityLayer where your agent runs, in a dev container, WSL2 or on a server. Its pages open in the browser on your computer through one forwarded port](pathname:///img/diagrams/remote-light.svg) ![Install QualityLayer where your agent runs, in a dev container, WSL2 or on a server. Its pages open in the browser on your computer through one forwarded port](pathname:///img/diagrams/remote-dark.svg) Install QualityLayer where your agent runs. No App is needed there, and you can [work only in your agent](work-in-your-agent.mdx). ```bash curl -fsSL https://qualitylayer.dev/install.sh | bash ``` The pages open in your Windows browser. The pages open in your browser; VS Code forwards the port. In the App, [add the container as a machine](machines.mdx#second-machine). To keep QualityLayer and your agent's sign-in when the container is rebuilt, keep them in volumes: ```json title=".devcontainer/devcontainer.json" "mounts": [ "source=qualitylayer-${devcontainerId},target=/home/vscode/.qualitylayer,type=volume", "source=claude-${devcontainerId},target=/home/vscode/.claude,type=volume" ], "postCreateCommand": "sudo chown vscode ~/.qualitylayer ~/.claude && curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash && curl -fsSL https://qualitylayer.dev/install.sh | bash" ``` In the App, [add it as a machine](machines.mdx), which also installs QualityLayer there. In a browser, VS Code Remote-SSH forwards the port for you; with plain `ssh`, forward the port that `qualitylayer app pair` prints. ### A port for each machine {#port} Machines added in **Settings › Machines** need no port of yours. In a browser, the server listens on port 41888 (41910 on WSL2), or the next free one. Two remote machines cannot both forward to 41888 on your laptop, so give each its own: ```bash qualitylayer settings set cockpit.port 41901 # on the server qualitylayer app restart ssh -N -L 41901:127.0.0.1:41901 first-server # on your laptop ``` Then open `http://127.0.0.1:41901`. `QUALITYLAYER_PORT=41901 qualitylayer app restart` tries a port once without saving it ([Server settings](reference/settings.mdx#server)). ## Updates {#updates} In the App, choose **Restart and update** from **Update ready** or the bar above the page. Without the App, run `qualitylayer update`; if a 12.x install finds no update, run the installation command again. Choose **Stable** or **Beta** in [Settings › About](reference/settings.mdx#about). ## Remove it {#uninstall} `qualitylayer uninstall` undoes what the installer changed; your plans stay. Add `--purge` to remove QualityLayer's settings, licence and tasks too. This works even when the App or command line is blocked or gone. Your plans, logins, licence and tasks stay; add `-Purge` to remove QualityLayer's settings, licence and tasks too. ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://qualitylayer.dev/install.ps1))) -Uninstall ``` To move your licence, run `qualitylayer licence activate ` on the other computer. A key works on 5 computers ([Licence](reference/settings.mdx#licence)). ## Windows with Intune or Defender Exploit Guard {#managed-windows} If Defender Exploit Guard blocks Setup or removes installed files, check your managed-device policy with IT. | Fix | How | | --- | --- | | **Exclusion** (IT) | Exclude `%LOCALAPPDATA%\QualityLayer` and `%USERPROFILE%\.qualitylayer\bin` (Intune: *Attack Surface Reduction Only Exclusions*) | | **File indicator** (IT) | Allow the setup file by its SHA-256 from `SHA256SUMS` on the release page | | **WSL** (no IT) | Install [in WSL2](#without-a-screen) | Then run `qualitylayer doctor` and open the App once. If code health setup fails because antivirus holds its tools, see [Setup under antivirus](reference/antivirus.mdx).

You approve twice: the Plan and the finished change. ## Start here The App for macOS, Windows and Linux, or the CLI for a server. Plan, build and review one small change. Start and answer tasks from your agent's own session. ## The three steps {#the-three-steps} ![The workflow from Plan to the pull request; you approve the Plan and the finished change, and merge](pathname:///img/diagrams/flow-pr-light.svg) ![The workflow from Plan to the pull request; you approve the Plan and the finished change, and merge](pathname:///img/diagrams/flow-pr-dark.svg) Your agent reads the code, asks what only you can answer and writes the Plan. **You approve it.** Your agent cuts the Plan into slices and builds each one test first. You create and merge the [pull request](steps/pull-request.mdx). ## Kinds of task {#choose-how-to-work} Something new, through the three steps. Start fresh or from a plan you already have. The three steps; the Plan names the cause and starts with a failing test. A conversation without steps. Move it into the workflow when it grows. ## Your agents {#who-it-is-for} Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Antigravity, Pi, OpenCode and GitHub Copilot [run natively](agents/native.mdx). Any other agent [uses the CLI](agents/other.mdx). Each keeps its own login and provider. Each task leaves `01-plan.md`, `02-implement.md` and `03-verify.md` in your repository. pages.machines.mdx: --- title: Machines description: Run agents on a Mac Mini, a Linux server or a VS Code dev container, and manage them from the App on your laptop. mdx: format: mdx --- import { Card, CardGroup, Steps, Step, Tabs, Tab, Tip, Note, Screenshot, Flow, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit"; Run tasks on a Mac Mini, a Linux server or a dev container, and follow them from the App on your laptop. Agents there keep working while your laptop sleeps. ## What you need macOS or Linux, with Git and your repository. Your ssh key, or the machine's password once. QualityLayer stores no password. Each machine counts as one of your licence's 5 computers. ## Add a machine {#second-machine} **Remote Login** under System Settings › General › Sharing. It is the one switch you make by hand. Install `openssh-server`. **Settings › Machines › Add machine**, or **Add machine** in the sidebar's switch. Under **Computer**, type `user@host` (`user@host:port` works), or pick a Mac from **Nearby** or a host from your ssh config, then **Add**. One progress view runs the steps: Reachable, Key, ssh config, System, QualityLayer, Licence, Connect. **Hide** keeps it going; **Settings › Machines** shows it again with **Show**. If the machine accepts no key of yours, QualityLayer makes `~/.ssh/qualitylayer_ed25519` and asks for the machine's password once, in a sheet that shows the host key it trusts. The password goes straight to ssh and is never stored. A machine that takes keys only shows a `ssh-copy-id` command to run once, then **Done · try again**. Choose **Open mac-mini** when pairing finishes. On its Setup page, choose **Install** or **Sign in** beside your agent. Sign-in opens the machine’s terminal in the App. Select a repository found on the machine, or enter its path, then choose **Start a task**. If your own key already works, nothing is asked. Pairing preserves your existing ssh settings and adds only its own marked configuration and trusted host key. **Reopen in Container** in VS Code, or `devcontainer up --workspace-folder .` with the [Dev Container CLI](https://github.com/devcontainers/cli). QualityLayer never starts or rebuilds containers. **Add machine › Dev container** lists the running containers from Docker Desktop, OrbStack, Colima or Podman. One that publishes ssh (container port 2222 or 22) adds with **Add**, without a password. A container without ssh shows **Needs ssh** with the lines to copy into its `devcontainer.json`: the sshd feature, a free port and a volume for its home. Rebuild it, then **Add**. Open the container’s Setup page to install or sign in to your agent. Select a repository or enter a path such as `/workspaces/api`, then choose **Start a task**. A rebuilt container pairs again by itself. ## Work on the machine {#work} With the machine chosen, start a task with **+** as on your laptop. The agent runs on the machine, and its Terminal pane shows it here. Its questions open as cards in the App. Approve the Plan with **Approve and build here**. Open a shell on the machine (`ssh mac-mini`), go to the project and ask your agent: "Using QualityLayer, plan …". The first time, it asks [where you answer and approve](work-in-your-agent.mdx#where). With **In the App**, questions and approvals come to the App on your laptop, under the machine. Change it later on the machine in **Settings › Workflow**. What waits on another machine raises the count on the sidebar's head. Its notification names the machine first: "mac-mini: Show greet version: Plan ready". ## Remove a machine {#remove} Under **Settings › Machines**, choose **Remove**. **Remove QualityLayer's key from it and its ssh config entry here** is on; tick **Also release its licence**, so the machine stops counting against your licence. Do this before you delete a container. ## When something is off {#troubleshooting} A step that fails shows its cause and its fix in the progress view; **Try again** resumes there. For a machine already added: | What you see | What to do | | --- | --- | | **No answer since 14:02 · Next try in 0:45** | Wait, or choose **Try now**. | | **Key refused** | **Pair again**. | | **Host key changed** | Compare the new fingerprint it shows, then **Trust new key**. | | The agent waits at "Trust this folder?" | Answer in the task's Terminal pane in the App, or in your own session on the machine. Each agent asks once per folder. | | An agent shows **Not installed** or not signed in on the machine's Setup page | Choose **Install** or **Sign in** beside it. **Check again** refreshes its status. | By command, `qualitylayer machines add user@host` asks for the password hidden, and a script pipes it with `--password-stdin`; `qualitylayer machines add --container ` adds a dev container ([all machine commands](reference/commands.mdx#machines)).

--- title: Project memory description: Save lessons about each project and how you work, and choose what travels through Git. mdx: format: mdx --- import { Card, CardGroup, Steps, Step, Tip, Note, Warning, Screenshot, Flow, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit"; Save decisions, fixes, constraints and working preferences for your agents to reuse, such as "Keep database migrations short and retry busy locks." ## What your agents get {#what-your-agents-get} Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Grok and GitHub Copilot receive pinned and matching lessons, and all but Grok again after compaction. `memory_search`, `memory_read`, `memory_save` and `memory_keep`; Antigravity and any other agent use the [command line](#command-line). Verify records decisions, fixed findings and amendments, never without recorded passing checks. A changed file marks a lesson for rechecking. If hooks are off, unavailable or too slow, delivery can be skipped; your agent searches when earlier decisions matter. The task's **Memory** record in **Files** shows what was used and saved. Lessons are reference data, never instructions: your agent checks them against the current code. ## Lessons about you {#lessons-about-you} Personal lessons apply across repositories on this computer and never go to Git. Find them under **Settings › Memory › Yours · every project**. ## Manage your lessons {#manage-your-lessons} In **Settings › Memory**, search, edit or retire lessons, and pin up to five per project and five personal ones. Use **Still true** after checking changed files. Stale lessons retire after 90 days and can be restored. **Lessons in every session** turns off automatic delivery; you can also pause memory. ## What stays local {#what-stays-local} Lessons and the search model stay on your computer; no lesson goes to an embedding service. A lesson given to your agent becomes part of its context, and a cloud agent may send that context to its provider. Agent and session attribution stays local when lessons go to Git. ## Share lessons through Git {#share-lessons-through-git} In **Manage projects**, enable **Store project lessons in Git** for the repository. It is off by default and applies to this computer. **Export** writes eligible lessons to `docs/memories/` with a readable `LESSONS.md`, beside `docs/plans/`. The local store stays the source. Files in an older `.qualitylayer/memories/` move there on the next export; you commit the move. Review the files, then commit and push them yourself. Memory exchange never commits, pushes or pulls. Anyone who can read the repository can read exported lessons. Personal preferences, credentials, private task answers, Pilot imports and session attribution stay out, and a privacy filter checks the files, but review them anyway. Turning sharing off stops exchange and leaves committed files in place. ### Restore lessons from Git {#import-repository-records} Choose **Restore from repository** in the project where you want the lessons. Your agent treats them as untrusted until it checks them against the current code. Search, startup and export never import by themselves. Imports keep each lesson's history, and a missing file never retires a local lesson. If two computers changed the same lesson, both stay: choose one with **Compare versions** and **Use selected version** before you export again. ## Import Pilot lessons {#import-pilot-lessons} Pilot Shell memories import per project: see [From Pilot Shell](moving-from-pilot-shell.mdx#import-memories-per-project). ## Command line {#command-line}
Search, save, pin and sync from the command line ```sh qualitylayer memory context "database migration locks" --json qualitylayer memory store --title "Bound migration locks" --content "Keep migration locks short, because a waiting migration blocks every write." --kind pattern --file db/migrations --json qualitylayer memory store --about you --title "Prefer concise replies" --content "Keep replies short unless I ask for detail." --json qualitylayer memory pin --json qualitylayer memory share on --json qualitylayer memory export --json qualitylayer memory import --json qualitylayer memory conflicts --json qualitylayer memory reconcile --revision --candidate local --json ``` All commands: [reference](reference/commands.mdx#memory).

QualityLayer and Pilot Shell 11 can run side by side. Installing QualityLayer keeps Pilot Shell, its configuration and its tools. Version 11 remains the last Pilot Shell version.

## Update from Pilot Shell {#update-from-pilot-shell}

Run `pilot update` in a terminal. Pilot Shell shows the update from v11 to v12 with its release notes and asks **Update now?**. When you confirm:

<Steps>
  <Step title="The installer starts">It says that Pilot Shell is now QualityLayer and keeps working.</Step>
  <Step title="It installs QualityLayer">On a Mac, or Linux with a screen, the App and its command line. Over ssh, in WSL or in a container, the command line alone.</Step>
  <Step title="It connects your agents">It adds the QualityLayer skills to each agent it finds, such as Claude Code and Codex. Every download is checked against the signed release before anything is written.</Step>
  <Step title="The App opens">To finish setting up. If it cannot open a window, the installer says where the App is.</Step>
</Steps>

You can also [install QualityLayer](install.mdx) directly; the result is the same.

## Start using QualityLayer {#start-using-qualitylayer}

Ask your agent to plan or implement using QualityLayer or QL.

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="Active Pilot Shell licence" icon="badge-check">Nothing to do.</Card>
  <Card title="Older or unrecognised key" icon="key-round">Email [hello@qualitylayer.dev](mailto:hello@qualitylayer.dev) from your purchase address. Keep the key private.</Card>
  <Card title="No licence" icon="download">Start a 7-day trial, even if you used a Pilot Shell trial.</Card>
</CardGroup>

Repositories, code and Pilot plans stay in place. Choose **Existing plan** in a new Feature or Bugfix to reuse a plan's text; its workflow state is not imported.

## Import memories per project {#import-memories-per-project}

Open **Settings › Memory › Import from Pilot Shell**. Choose your Pilot memory folder, `pilot-memory.db`, a `.backup.json` or `.backup.gz` archive, or existing JSONL/Markdown exports. For a database, add the private knowledge folder separately if you want those documents too.

Review the records and choose a project or **Yours · every project** for each group. Saved lessons and knowledge summaries stay private; chats, prompts, tool activity, credentials and settings are excluded. Pilot files stay unchanged. If you stop, already imported lessons stay saved; retry the same source to import the rest without duplicates ([Pilot memory import](memory.mdx#import-pilot-lessons)).

## Remove Pilot Shell when you are ready {#remove-pilot-shell-when-you-are-ready}

Once your workflows work in QualityLayer, remove Pilot Shell with its own uninstaller:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maxritter/qualitylayer/main/uninstall.sh | bash
```

It asks before removing anything and keeps the tools Pilot Shell installed; add `--remove-tools` to remove those too.

<Note>QualityLayer never runs Pilot Shell's uninstaller or removes its tools for you.</Note>

title: Setup under antivirus
sidebar_label: Antivirus
description: What to do when quality setup fails on Windows because antivirus holds the new files.
mdx:

import { Steps, Step, Note, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

On Windows, antivirus that scans every new file can hold a tool QualityLayer has just downloaded. `qualitylayer quality setup` then fails for that tool.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Run setup again">Run `qualitylayer quality setup` again. It waits up to 30 seconds for the scan, then copies the files into place. Each tool installs on its own, so one failure leaves the others ready.</Step>
  <Step title="See what failed">Run `qualitylayer quality status`. It lists each tool and the last error. The full log is `%USERPROFILE%\.qualitylayer\quality-setup.log`.</Step>
  <Step title="Add an exclusion">If a tool still fails, add `%USERPROFILE%\.qualitylayer\tools` to your antivirus exclusions, or ask your IT team to. Then run `qualitylayer quality setup` once more.</Step>
</Steps>

<Note>Your tasks keep working meanwhile. Verify names a scanner that is not installed instead of failing the check.</Note>

---
title: Code health
description: Local checks for code complexity, duplication, secrets, vulnerable packages and risky code.
mdx:
  format: mdx
---

import { Card, CardGroup, Steps, Step, Tip, Note, Warning, Screenshot, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

QualityLayer checks code on your computer and gives the findings to your agent and its reviewers. Code health covers complexity and duplication; security scans cover secrets, vulnerable or malicious packages, unsafe workflows and risky code. Findings never stop the work.

<Screenshot name="code-health" alt="Verify's checks for the example task: project checks, security scans with two findings, the security review and the independent review" caption="An example task in a fictional project." />

## What happens as you work {#what-happens-as-you-work}

![Edited code is checked locally. Your agent reads each finding, fixes a problem or records why the code should stay. Tests verify the change.](pathname:///img/diagrams/code-health-light.svg)
![Edited code is checked locally. Your agent reads each finding, fixes a problem or records why the code should stay. Tests verify the change.](pathname:///img/diagrams/code-health-dark.svg)

<Steps>
  <Step title="Code is edited">At the end of each turn, edited files get a structure check and a secrets scan.</Step>
  <Step title="Your agent gets the findings">It reads the source and explains the consequence before changing anything.</Step>
  <Step title="It fixes or reviews each one">Fixes get the relevant tests; an intentional pattern keeps its review reason.</Step>
</Steps>

Checks never start another agent turn; findings reach your agent when the conversation next continues.

## Security scans {#security-scans}

In [Verify](../steps/verify.mdx#lanes), the scans read what the task changed, beside your project checks. Each reads only the files it knows:

| Scan | Reads | Tool |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Secrets | Every changed file | Betterleaks |
| Dependencies | A changed lockfile | OSV-Scanner |
| GitHub workflows | A changed workflow or action | zizmor |
| Code | Changed JavaScript, TypeScript and Python | OpenGrep, with QualityLayer's rules |

The Security review starts from the findings; the Independent review rules on them. A scan with no file to read is **not needed**. A scan that could not read a file says **not checked**, never clean.

Verify scans the task's registered commits and its recorded edits to tracked files; another task's changes stay outside. Untracked files are not scanned there, but the secrets scan after each agent turn still reads them. Secrets found in the task's records are removed before commit.

<Note>Only dependency advisories leave your computer: when a lockfile changes, its package names and versions are checked against osv.dev. Choose **Local copy** in [Settings](settings.mdx#security-scans) to keep them here; the database is about 250 MB.</Note>

## What a finding means {#what-a-finding-means}

| Finding | What your agent looks for |
| --- | --- |
| Complex function | Branches or responsibilities that make a change hard to follow |
| Duplicated code | Copies that could drift apart; broader duplication checks run when you ask |
| Possible secret | A key or password in a file; a real one is moved out and rotated |
| Advisory | A package version with a known vulnerability or known malware |
| Previously seen | A finding the tool already reported; it still needs review |
| Acknowledged | A finding kept with a specific reason; the code has not been repaired |

A finding needs a new review when its function, the analyzer configuration or its duplicate changes, or when its metric goes up.

## Ask for a broader check {#ask-for-a-broader-check}

Try "Check this project's duplication", "Review the complexity of the files we changed" or "Scan this branch for secrets." Your agent can also run your project's enabled linters.

<Warning>Code health and security scans are advisory: your tests and release requirements still apply. A failed, skipped or unavailable check never counts as passing.</Warning>

  { title: "Commands", href: "/docs/reference/commands#code-health", text: "Code health commands and setup troubleshooting." },
  { title: "Verify", href: "/docs/steps/verify", text: "Where the scans run beside your checks." },
]} />

---
title: Commands
description: Ask in plain language, or look up the CLI commands for tasks, artifacts, code health and memory.
mdx:
  format: mdx
---

import { Tip, Note, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

Ask your agent in plain words, or run the commands yourself. `qualitylayer help` (`ql` for short) lists them.

<Tip>Add `--json` for machine-readable output and `--task <slug>` to pick an open task.</Tip>

## Ask in plain words {#in-your-agent}

Name **QualityLayer** or **QL** in a plain request; your agent picks the [skill](../agents/native.mdx#the-six-skills).

| Example request | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| “Using QualityLayer, plan a CSV export” | Starts a task at [Plan](../steps/plan.mdx) |
| “Using QL, implement the approved plan for task retry-webhooks” | Builds an approved Plan ([Implement](../steps/implement.mdx#start-implement)) |
| “Using QL, review task retry-webhooks” | Reviews the result or follows [pull request](../steps/pull-request.mdx) review threads |
| “Open the current QualityLayer artifact in my browser at Billing” | Opens that artifact page and section |

## Existing plans {#existing-plans}

`qualitylayer task start "<request>" --from-plan ./plan.md` starts at Plan from an existing Markdown or plain-text plan. Use `-` for standard input. The original stays unchanged ([Plan](../steps/plan.mdx#a-bug)).

## From a ticket {#from-a-ticket}

`qualitylayer task start --from <link>` starts at Plan from a GitHub or GitLab issue or pull request, a Jira issue or a Confluence page, and the task keeps the link. QualityLayer reads GitHub and GitLab with your own `gh` or `glab`: the ticket's title and text become the request, and images and attachments stay links. It signs in to nothing itself, so your agent reads a Jira or Confluence link with its own tools. In the App, paste the link into New task.

For a GitHub.com repository, `qualitylayer gate open plan --via github` or **Pull request** in the App's header pushes the Plan on its own branch and opens GitHub's compare page with the title and description filled in. You create the pull request there. An approving review on it, by someone else with write access, approves the Plan, and every comment comes back to the agent as feedback. If you approve the Plan in QualityLayer instead, the pull request gets a note, closes and its branch is deleted.

For a GitHub.com repository, `qualitylayer gate open final --via github` or **Pull request** on Verify pushes the task's branch and opens GitHub's compare page with the Verify page as the description. An approving review there, by someone else with write access, approves the change, and its comments go to the agents as review feedback. Pull requests for approval work with GitHub only.

## Chat {#chat}

“Using QualityLayer, chat about retrying failed webhooks” starts a [Chat](../chat.mdx) with a supported coding agent.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `chat plan save --file <markdown>` | Save `chat-plan.md` (`--text` instead of a file) |
| `chat build [--file <cards>]` · `--stop <slice>` | Start or resume slice helpers, or record one stopped |
| `chat check [--slice <n>]` · `chat review` | Print validation commands, or brief a fresh reviewer |
| `chat promote --type feature\|bugfix [--from-saved-plan]` | Move into the workflow at Plan, from the conversation or the saved plan |

## Answer in your agent {#terminal-mode}

Keep a task's questions and approvals in your agent's chat. Only your own picks or words count ([In your agent](../work-in-your-agent.mdx)). The value `terminal` means your agent's chat.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `task set answers=terminal\|app` · `approvals=terminal\|app` | Where you answer and approve for the current task |
| `settings set answers terminal` · `settings set approvals terminal` | Where tasks you start in your agent answer and approve |
| `settings set offerWorkflow false` | Your agent no longer offers QualityLayer when you ask it to plan |
| `read 01-plan.md [--lead]` · `read artifact <name>` | Read a document or artifact page as text |
| `plan export --out <folder>` | Export the Plan, its agents' file and pictures; report any picture that could not be made |

## Commands by group {#commands-by-group}

Prefix each command with `qualitylayer`, for example `qualitylayer gate open plan`.

| Group | Commands |
| --- | --- |
| [Step checks](settings.mdx#step-checks) | `instructions` · `instructions add <step> "<line>"` · `instructions done\|skip <step> <n>` |
| [Automations](../automations.mdx) | `automations list` · `automations add --url <url> \| --command "<command>"` · `automations set\|remove\|test\|log\|secret <id>` · `automations events` |
| Tasks | `find` · `tasks` · `status` · `task set` · `task start` · `task override` · `task archive\|restore` · `branch new` |
| App | `app` · `app status` · `app restart` · `agents list\|check\|repair` |
| Setup | `doctor [--repair]` · `settings get\|set` · `update` · `uninstall [--purge | --keep-data]` · `reset --first-start` · `licence status\|activate\|deactivate\|portal` · `feedback` |
| Settings | `settings set <key> <value>` changes any setting except the permission mode, the program an agent or terminal starts and its arguments, and who may type; those stay in the App's Settings |
| Usage | `usage import cursor <file.csv> --from <ISO time> --to <ISO time> [--account <local label>]`: import a local CSV; import again to add later usage |

<details>
<summary>Workflow commands your agent runs</summary>

| Group | Commands |
| --- | --- |
| Workflow | `next` (reads only) · `brief plan\|implement\|verify` · `task start` · `plan draft` · `gate open plan\|final` · `plan amend` · `plan export` · `wait`. `wait --for approval --until-decided` returns on a decision, a comment, a review to address, a saved answer to fold in, or timeout. |
| Questions | `question ask` · `question show` · `question answered` · `question link` |
| Building | `build start` · `build done` · `check task T<n>\|slice <n>\|step A<n>\|all` · `commit slice <n>\|slices\|fix [--commit <hash>]\|task [--diff <file>]` · `card T<n>` · `need "<what. why>" --for T<n>` · `limit add` · `progress` |
| Checking | `verify judge\|recheck\|fix\|keep-red` · `verdict` · `verdict finish` · `verdict run` · `attest` · `evidence shot` · `validate` |
| Shipping | `ship` · `pr watch` |

For a second checkout, add a line such as `` - **Repository:** `/work/evaluation` `` under **Scope → In scope** before Plan approval. Use that exact checkout with `check task T<n> --repo /work/evaluation` and `commit slice <n> --repo /work/evaluation --commit <hash>`.

</details>

## Artifacts {#artifacts}

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `artifact new <name> [--wire] [--folder] [--on <artifact>]` | Start an artifact, wireframe, multi-page folder, or draft on a lasting artifact |
| `artifact show\|open <name> [--page <page>] [--section <id>] [--browser]` | Show the latest version, or open an exact page |
| `artifact keep <name> [--only-here]` | Make a draft a lasting artifact |
| `artifact list` | List local artifacts |
| `artifact check\|shot <name> [--page <page>]` · `artifact review <name>` | Check the HTML, take pictures, or brief a design check |
| `artifact tokens <name> [--refresh]` | Fix values that differ from the project's design file |
| `artifact library inspect\|rename\|copy\|archive\|restore\|delete <name>` | Manage lasting artifacts |

Artifact edits take `--if-match <revision>` from `artifact inspect` or `artifact library inspect`. `artifact shot` and `artifact check --render` need Chrome.

## Code health and security scans {#code-health}

Advisory local checks ([Code health](code-health.mdx)).

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `quality check [paths...] [--all] [--duplication] [--fail-on-new]` | Check changed and untracked, or named, source |
| `quality scan [paths... \| --since <rev>] [--secrets\|--dependencies\|--workflows\|--code] [--local]` | Scan changed or named files for secrets, vulnerable packages, unsafe workflows and risky code |
| `quality metrics\|lint [paths...]` | Function metrics, or the project's linters |
| `quality acknowledge <id> --reason "<evidence>"` | Keep a reviewed finding with its reason |
| `quality status\|setup\|on\|off` | Status reports the retained checkout folder in `reportDirectory` with `--json`. Setup reinstalls the quality tools. Use on and off to resume or pause automatic checks. On Windows, see [Setup under antivirus](antivirus.mdx). |

## Project memory {#memory}

One local lesson store for the App and your agents ([Project memory](../memory.mdx)).

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `memory overview\|list\|search <text>\|read <id>` | Browse lessons; `--scope repo\|you` picks this project or yours. `list --sources changed` shows lessons whose files changed |
| `memory store --title <text> --content <text>` | Save a lesson; `--file`, `--rests-on` and `--replaces <id>` add context. `--about you` saves a personal lesson for every repository |
| `memory confirm\|retire <id> [--reason <text>]` | Confirm a lesson at the current commit, or retire it. Personal lessons have no commit to confirm against |
| `memory pin\|unpin\|restore <id>` | Keep a lesson in every session, or restore a retired one |
| `memory pause\|resume` · `memory sessions on\|off` | Pause capture, or session lessons |
| `memory share on\|off` · `memory export` | Opt into project Git export, or write eligible records; never commits, pushes or pulls |
| `memory import` | Explicitly import repository records; differs from restoring a retired local lesson |
| `memory conflicts` · `memory reconcile <id> --revision <n> --candidate local\|<fingerprint>` | Inspect conflicting revisions and explicitly reconcile them |
| `memory mcp` · `memory import-pilot <file>…` | Serve lesson tools over MCP, or import Pilot records |

## Machines {#machines}

Other computers and dev containers you reach over ssh ([Machines](../machines.mdx)).

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `machines add user@host [--name <n>] [--trust SHA256:…]` | Pair a computer. It asks for the password hidden when no key of yours works; a script pipes it with `--password-stdin`, never as an argument |
| `machines add --container <name>` | Pair a running dev container |
| `machines containers` · `machines snippet [--port <n>]` · `machines nearby` | Running dev containers, the `devcontainer.json` lines that give one ssh, and Macs nearby that offer ssh |
| `machines list` · `machines status <name>` | Your machines, and how one is reached |
| `machines pair\|retry <name>` | Pair a machine again, or try one that is down now |
| `machines trust <name> [--fingerprint …]` | Trust a machine's changed host key |
| `machines rename <name> <new>` · `machines remove <name> [--release] [--keep-key]` | Rename one, or remove it; `--release` frees its licence, `--keep-key` leaves QualityLayer's key on it |

## Session messaging {#session-messaging}

To oversee a task, ask your agent to run `qualitylayer status --json --task <task>` from its checkout. Read the task documents for verification evidence.

| Status field | What it reports |
| --- | --- |
| `waiting_on` | A human action, agent or helper work, or unknown activity. Native permission requests use `reason: agent_permission` |
| `last_decision` | Approvals and requested changes |
| `answer_mode` | Where you answer, with its recorded origin |

<Note>Sessions on this computer coordinate through `ql-peer` within the work you authorize. You choose the build session and approve the Plan and the finished change.</Note>

```bash
qualitylayer peers list
qualitylayer peers send --to 'cc:<name-or-uuid>' --message-file ./review-request.txt --json
```

Address `cc:`, `codex:`, `pi:`, `opencode:`, `copilot:`, `grok:`, `cursor:` or `antigravity:` plus a name or UUID. `peers help` lists the reply commands; `peers doctor` finds a missing session.

GitHub Copilot, Grok, Cursor and Antigravity sessions join the list at their first hook. Messages arrive:

- At once in a waiting App session.
- At turn end or the next prompt while the agent works.
- At the next turn in an idle session.

  { title: "Settings", href: "/docs/reference/settings", text: "Every setting, in the App and by command." },
  { title: "Automations", href: "/docs/automations", text: "Task events for your own tools and scripts." },
