---
title: Files and privacy
description: What a task writes into your repository, what stays on your computer, and what leaves it.
mdx:
  format: mdx
---

import { Note, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

What a task writes into your repository, what stays on your computer, and what leaves it.

## A task's files {#a-tasks-files}

![A task folder in docs/plans: three documents with their agents' files, local interactive artifacts, reviews, command output, and evidence pictures and recordings](pathname:///img/diagrams/files-light.svg)
![A task folder in docs/plans: three documents with their agents' files, local interactive artifacts, reviews, command output, and evidence pictures and recordings](pathname:///img/diagrams/files-dark.svg)

Each task gets a folder in `docs/plans/`: plain Markdown, kept on disk and never touched by uninstalling.

<Note>You decide whether to commit these documents; QualityLayer never stages or commits them by itself.</Note>

| In the folder | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| **The three documents** | One per step, each with a file for agents ([below](#documents)) |
| `research/` | The helpers' reports, one per question |
| `original-plan.md` | A plan supplied through Existing plan or saved in Chat, unchanged |
| `artifacts/` | Local artifacts and their revisions. |
| `reviews/` | The Plan review and second opinion, when they ran; with a panel, also each reviewer's answer of both rounds |
| `records/` | Check results in `checks.md`, command output, and `pull-request-body.md`. Open check results in **Files › Records › Checks** |
| `evidence/` | Pictures and recordings the checks made |
| `chat-plan.md`, `chat-slices.md` | A [Chat](../chat.mdx)'s saved plan and its build outline |

## The three documents {#documents}

Each opens with what you read first. Code shapes, paths and commands follow in the Reader.

<Note>QualityLayer refuses a document whose marked sections were edited by hand.</Note>

| File | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `01-plan.md` | What you approve: the problem, **Done means** with their steps, scope, diagrams, artifacts, the approach and the decisions. Its front matter holds the task's identity |
| `agents/01-plan.md` | Notes for the build: constraints, findings, code to follow, how to run and test, pitfalls. It grants nothing; the Plan wins |
| `02-implement.md` | The slices, what was decided while building and known limits |
| `agents/02-implement.md` | The task cards and the build's notes |
| `03-verify.md` | The pull request's description: why, the code, the change in diagrams, the screens and **Done means** as it ran |
| `agents/03-verify.md` | Verdicts, findings, commands, security review, fix rounds, ship steps and follow-ups |

## Lasting artifacts {#lasting}

| Location | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `.qualitylayer/artifacts/<name>/` | A [lasting artifact](../artifacts.mdx#keep) and its `artifact.json`, committed with the change (older `.qualitylayer/designs/` still read) |
| `docs/artifacts/` | Artifacts kept only on this computer, out of git |
| `docs/memories/` | Project lessons you [export](../memory.mdx) to Git, with a readable `LESSONS.md`; you commit them |
| `~/.qualitylayer/project-look.json` | Sidebar order, colors, names and hidden projects. Delete it to reset |

## What stays on your computer, and what leaves it {#privacy}

Your code, diff, documents, evidence, memories and costs stay on machines you control. Your chosen agent may send its context to its provider under your account and settings.

| Destination | What is sent |
| --- | --- |
| **Licence and trial service** | A licence check, activation or trial request with the identifiers needed for entitlement. Existing trial dates and the offline allowance stay unchanged |
| **Downloads and updates** | Requests for the official App, CLI, update information and release notes |
| **Your coding agent** | Your request, project instructions and relevant context, through the agent's native integration |
| **Automations** | Task events, including titles and question text, to the URL or command you explicitly configure. Nothing passes through qualitylayer.dev |
| **Your own Git remote** | Files you authorize committing and pushing, including optional project [memory exports](../memory.mdx). Repository readers can read them |
| **Your own remote machine or paired browser** | Your local work over the authenticated connection you configure; no hosted collaboration workspace is created |
| **Support** | The report, diagnostics and screenshots you review before sending, through the separate product-support service |

Official releases contain their matching readable workflow instructions, templates, schemas and skills locally. Running a workflow does not download instructions from a hosted store. Licensing remains required; public instruction text is not a free product licence.

Personal lessons, private session attribution, credentials, transcripts and terminal streams stay outside project memory exports. Existing tasks, question answers, approval records, artifacts and sessions remain local. Retired annotations and attachments are read-only private records; they never grant approval or create a new agent message.

Older clients can continue to use retained services during migration. The [privacy policy](https://qualitylayer.dev/privacy) describes that transitional processing separately. An upgrade does not itself delete remote records or shorten existing retention obligations.

## Report a problem {#feedback}

**Report bug / idea** in the sidebar foot (**Bug / idea** in a narrower sidebar) files a public issue on `maxritter/qualitylayer`: add a title, description and screenshots, choose **Preview public issue**, then **Create public GitHub issue**. Use **Private support** for confidential details. The report adds QualityLayer, operating-system and architecture details and the agent version; it does not add your account name, email, repository paths or terminal logs.

---
title: Settings
description: Configure your workflow, agents, memory, usage and updates.
mdx:
  format: mdx
---

import { Tip, Note, Screenshot, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

Open **Settings** with the gear at the bottom of the sidebar; its search finds any setting. Changes save at once for this computer.

<Screenshot name="settings" alt="Settings: its sections in the sidebar's place, with your instructions, where you answer and approve, and the reviews in Workflow" />

<Tip>Every setting also works by command, `qualitylayer settings set <key> <value>`, or by asking your agent. The [command reference](commands.mdx#commands-by-group) lists the few that stay in the App.</Tip>

## Workflow {#workflow}

| Setting | Choices |
| --- | --- |
| **Offer QualityLayer** | A switch: on (default), your agent asks once when you ask it to plan without naming QualityLayer |
| [Your instructions](#instructions) | Standing instructions for every task |
| **Answer questions in** · **Approve in** | **In the App** (default) or **In my own agent**: your terminal, IDE or agent app, for tasks you start there ([guide](../work-in-your-agent.mdx#where)) |
| [Independent review](#independent-review) | A switch: on (recommended) or off. Runs in Verify and each recheck |
| **Design review** | A switch: on (default), a separate agent checks each finished design in Plan before you see it. Wireframes are never reviewed |
| [Second opinion](#second-opinion) | A switch: off (default); it turns on once a second coding agent is installed. Runs in Plan and Verify |
| [Scan each change](#security-scans) | A switch: on (default) or off |
| [Dependency advisories](#security-scans) | **osv.dev** (default) or **Local copy** |

Each review row lists the model every installed agent uses for it; click a model to change it in [Models](#models).

### Your instructions {#instructions}

Write up to 12,000 characters in `~/.qualitylayer/instructions.md`. Agents, helpers and reviewers read it each step; documents never copy it. Headings such as `## Plan` and `## Implement` limit lines to that step; a checkbox (`- [ ]`) under one is a [step check](#step-checks). Instructions cannot approve a gate.

#### Step checks {#step-checks}

A step check is a checkbox line under a step's heading. The agent must do it, then record it done or skipped with a reason.

```md
## Verify
- [ ] run: `wizcli dir scan --path .`
- [ ] Review auth changes with the threat-model skill
- Mention Wiz findings in the pull request.
```

| Line | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| `- [ ] run: …` under Implement or Verify | A Project check: the Plan names it, approving the Plan covers running it, and [Verify](../steps/verify.mdx) records its result |
| `- [ ]` with other words | The agent does it its own way, with a skill, an MCP tool or by hand, and records a note or a reason |
| `-` a plain bullet | Guidance only |

Add one in **Your instructions** › **Steps**, ask your agent (“Add a Wiz scan to Verify's step checks”), or run `qualitylayer instructions add verify "<line>"`. A task keeps the checks it started with; skipped ones stay in its record. Commands use the logins already on your computer.

### Independent review {#independent-review}

**On**: a separate agent checks each **Done means** point in [Verify](../steps/verify.mdx). **Helpers: This session** in [Models](#models) keeps review in the lead session, marked as not independent. **Off**: Verify shows **Independent review** as **skipped**. [Models](#models) sets the model each agent reviews on.

### Second opinion {#second-opinion}

**On** adds a read-only review by another agent for risky Plans and changes. Risk includes sign-in, secrets, outside input, or a Plan or slice marked risky. The Workflow row shows which agent reviews which. In [Models](#models) you pick, for each agent, the other installed agent that reviews its work and the model it uses. The default is the first agent here from another model family, so GPT reviews Claude and Claude reviews GPT. If the chosen agent is not installed or not signed in, the default reviews instead. Your agent can set it too: `qualitylayer settings set secondOpinion.reviewers.claude-code '{"agent":"codex","model":"gpt-6.1-sol"}'`.

<Note>A feature can also take up to two extra planners, each an agent, model and effort, chosen in **New task** or with `qualitylayer task start "<request>" --planners agent:model[:effort],…`. They review its Plan instead of the second opinion, and each is an extra paid planning run.</Note>

<details>
<summary>How the default reviewer is picked</summary>

- Pi and OpenCode count by the model they run; Cursor's Auto never counts as another family.
- Agents that enforce read-only come first, then Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Pi, OpenCode, Cursor, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot. Cursor and Antigravity review a disposable copy.
- When every agent here runs the same family, a fresh session reviews on its agent’s second-opinion model. **Reviewed by** in the Plan names who read it.

</details>

### Security scans {#security-scans}

**Scan each change** runs the [security scans](code-health.mdx#security-scans) in Verify and the secrets scan after each agent turn. **Off**: Verify's Security scans lane says Off; the reviews still run.

**Dependency advisories**: **osv.dev** sends the package names and versions of a changed lockfile to Google's open vulnerability database; your code stays here. **Local copy** downloads that database (about 250 MB for npm and PyPI) the first time a project needs it, and nothing leaves this computer.

## Agents {#defaults}

**On this computer** shows each agent's version, sign-in, integration check and **Use** switch. Problems offer **Repair**, **Out of date** or **Not installed**.

- The model button on the row, or **⋯ › Models**, opens [Models](#models) on that agent.
- **Install…** opens the vendor's page; QualityLayer never runs an installer.

| **⋯ › Edit launch…** | What it changes |
| --- | --- |
| **Command** | The program's absolute path. `QUALITYLAYER_CODEX_BIN`-style variables win over it |
| **Extra arguments** | Added to every start; ones that switch off permission checks are refused |
| **Config folder** | Where the agent keeps its settings |
| **Default effort** | High is recommended; a per-task choice wins |
| **Default permission mode** | Bypass on first use; your saved mode or **Agent settings** wins ([modes](../agents/native.mdx#permission-modes)) |

Only the App, or a browser paired with its key, can change these.

Under **Another agent**, enter a command name or path in **Program** and any optional flags in **Arguments**. **Save** keeps both settings together.

### What setup sets {#what-setup-sets}

Setup adds each of these only when it is missing, next to QualityLayer's own hooks. Your own values stay, and `qualitylayer uninstall` takes back only what it set.

| Agent | Settings |
| --- | --- |
| **Claude Code** permissions | Bypass by default, without its confirmation screen. Existing native and managed policies remain authoritative |
| **Claude Code** git | No attribution in commits or pull requests; no built-in git instructions |
| **Claude Code** display | Concise replies, thinking summaries, reduced motion, flicker-free screen |
| **Claude Code** tools | Task tools, tool search, baseline task reminders, memory consolidation where Claude makes it available, at most 3 Stop-hook continuations in a row, High effort |
| **Codex** | Full access when no permission policy is set, High effort for the session and subagents, the model's largest context window, its question picker |
| **Grok** | Questions wait for your answer instead of expiring after 30 minutes |

## Models {#models}

Pick an agent by its mark. A fresh setup recommends Opus in Claude Code and GPT-6.2 Astra in Codex and Pi for planning and reviews. OpenCode starts on its own settings and recommends Astra for reviews. Saved choices still apply, and each launch can pick another model. Each group's **Reset to recommended** restores its own rows.

| Group | Rows |
| --- | --- |
| **Plan and Implement** | **Plan**, **Implement · full task**, **Implement · small change**, **Implement subagents** (Codex and Claude Code) and **Helpers** for research, fixes, security checks and Chat work. **This session** keeps helper work in the lead session |
| **Reviews** | **Independent review**: the model a fresh helper checks this agent's change on. **Design review**: the model a fresh helper checks this agent's designs on. **Second opinion**: the other installed agent that reads this agent's risky work, and its model. Each works by command too, such as `qualitylayer settings set models.codex.design gpt-6.1-sol` |
| **Model list** | Open the selected agent’s catalog to see the models assigned to roles. Search by name or id, or choose **Show all** to browse. **Add a model…** takes an id the agent accepts. **Remove** puts its roles back on the recommended model |

## Usage {#usage}

**Usage display** defaults to **Used**; **Remaining** changes both the App and macOS menu bar. Menu bar usage starts on.

| Control | What it changes |
| --- | --- |
| **Menu bar readings** | Reported quota windows and daily dollars. Quota choices also select the Usage popup's rows |
| **Daily total** | Optional: **API spend ($)** counts metered use; **All usage at API prices ($)** also values subscriptions for comparison |

Credits stay separate in Usage; missing data makes totals partial. The task header’s [Cost](../app.mdx#cost) uses recorded Copilot AI-credit usage value where available, clearly labelled separately from API-price estimates and money billed.

**Plan limits** shows reported windows for Claude Code, Codex and GitHub Copilot. Visible readings refresh every five minutes; Codex and Copilot depend on their latest source records. **Resume when a limit resets** (on) continues stopped builds unless someone has typed since; **Cancel resume** in the task's agent status stops one.

**What your agents used** has daily charts, comparisons and model breakdowns for 7 days, 30 days or this month. Every supported agent is covered where its records provide usage; Cursor needs a [local CSV import](commands.mdx#commands-by-group). The same money choice applies to statistics. API-price value is not your bill.

## Sessions {#sessions}

**Running now** lists running agents; **Stop N idle** stops the idle ones, which keep their conversation. Stopping several asks for confirmation.

| Setting | Choices |
| --- | --- |
| **Stop agents that sit idle** | Never, 2 h, 8 h (default) or a day; never one with an open question, approval, turn or helper |
| **Who can type in a session** | **The App and its browsers** (default), or also other paired browsers |
| **When you quit the App** | **Agents keep running** (default) or **Stop agents** |

## Machines {#machines}

Work on another Linux or macOS computer, or a dev container, you reach over ssh, from this App ([setup guide](../machines.mdx)). **Add machine** takes `user@host`, a Mac nearby, a host from your ssh config or a running dev container; **Add** pairs it in one progress view, installs QualityLayer there and activates your licence key on it. It asks for the machine's password at most once and stores none. The sidebar's head then switches between **This computer** and each machine, with a count of what waits for you elsewhere.

A machine keeps working while this computer sleeps and reconnects by itself. A machine that is down says why and offers its fix: **Try now**, **Pair again** for a refused key, or **Trust new key** with the new fingerprint. **Remove…** also takes QualityLayer's key off the machine and its ssh config entry here, unless you clear that; tick **Also release its licence** to free the machine's activation. Windows machines keep their own App.

## Notifications {#notifications}

**Tell me when a task needs me** enables system notifications; **Play a sound with it** adds sound.

Use your own connected machine or paired browser to return to your work away from this computer.

## Git and editor {#git-and-editor}

**Commit timing** sets the default for new tasks. Choose **After each checked slice**, **Once before Verify** or **After I review the diff**. During Implement, a task can change timing for its next commit. Verify checks the resulting commit. A separate repository approved in the Plan keeps its own checks and commit registration. **Tools** shows whether Git and `gh` are signed in; without `gh`, no pull requests. **Open files and folders in** picks the editor or system app to use. For a **Custom editor**, enter its program and any arguments, one per line, then select **Save editor**. QualityLayer adds the file or folder path as the last argument. **Watch pull requests** (on) wakes the task's agent on a failing check, change request or conflict, at most 3 times a day per pull request, and on people's new review comments up to 2 more times, never below 10 % of the plan left.

## Automations {#automations}

Send task events to a URL or a command. A browser that may only watch cannot change them. See [Automations](../automations.mdx).

## Appearance {#appearance}

| Setting | Choices |
| --- | --- |
| **Theme** | System, Light or Dark |
| **Text size** | 90%, 100% (default), 115% or 130% for the installed App window. ⌘+/⌘− resize; ⌘0 resets (Ctrl on Windows/Linux). A browser tab uses its own zoom |
| **Font** | Geist (default), System or Atkinson Hyperlegible. Code, paths and the agent terminal keep their own fonts |
| **Show agent sessions as** | **Conversation** or **Terminal** for new sessions |
| **Messages while working** | In **Agent controls › Appearance…**: **Steer at next step** (default) or **Queue until the turn ends**; unsupported agents queue without interrupting |
| **Task rows** | Detailed, Two lines or One line |
| **Agent terminal** | **Font size** and **Colours** stay in view; **More terminal settings** holds font, weight, spacing, cursor and scrollback. **Reset to recommended** restores defaults |

## Memory {#memory}

Pause, search or retire lessons, including **Yours**, the lessons about you. **Manage projects** controls optional Git export per repository ([Project memory](../memory.mdx)).

## Licence {#licence}

Your plan or trial, and **Open billing account**. To use a key you bought, choose **Enter key…** (during the trial too) and paste it from your billing account; Setup offers the same field. From a terminal, run `qualitylayer licence activate <key>`; on Windows before the command is set up, run `& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\QualityLayer\qualitylayer-cli.exe" licence activate <key>` in PowerShell. Each licence key works on 5 computers, [machines](#machines) included; on Business, every assigned seat has its own key. **On another computer** shows how to move the licence. When all 5 are in use, release one under **Licence keys** in your billing account, run `qualitylayer licence deactivate` on the old computer, or write to hello@qualitylayer.dev.


## About {#about}

The version, **Check now** and **Update channel**: **Stable** (default) or **Beta**, which also moves to each newer stable release ([Updates](../install.mdx#updates)).

### Server {#server}

**Server port** is 41888 unless you change it (1024 to 65535); type one and **Restart on N**. **In use now** shows the real port, for example "41888 was taken, so it uses 41889." `QUALITYLAYER_PORT` overrides it for one server; `qualitylayer settings set cockpit.port <port>` sets it from the command line.

## For one task {#for-one-task}

Tell your agent "skip security", "run the security review", "get a second opinion" or "no second opinion".

<Note>No setting turns an approval off.</Note>

import { Card, CardGroup, Steps, Step, Tabs, Tab, Tip, Note, Screenshot, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

Your agent cuts the approved Plan into slices and builds each one test first. You start the build, and it runs on its own.

<Screenshot name="implement" alt="Implement in the App: the slices and their progress, beside the agent's conversation" caption="An example task in a fictional project." />

## Start the build {#start-implement}

<Tabs groupId="where">
  <Tab value="app" label="In the App">

**Approve and build here** continues the planning session after its turn, keeping its model and effort. **Start the build** on Plan opens the build card for a new session:

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Agent" icon="square-terminal">The coding agent for this build, with **What's different** for that agent.</Card>
  <Card title="Build model and Effort" icon="code-xml">For Codex and Claude Code, the saved full-task or small-change model is selected. You can change the model or effort for this build.</Card>
  <Card title="Subagent model" icon="network">For Codex and Claude Code, the model any subagents use. The lead usually builds small changes itself.</Card>
  <Card title="Files and Workspace" icon="file-text">Attachments, where it runs, and the [branch or worktree](#where-it-lands).</Card>
</CardGroup>

Press **Approve & start**. Closing the sidebar keeps the run ([agent runs](../app.mdx#agent-runs)).

  </Tab>
  <Tab value="agent" label="In my own agent">

A planner waiting in your own agent shows **Build in <agent> · your agent**: run your agent's compact command, then say "build here".

Otherwise the card shows one request box with **Copy** and a folder chip. Paste the request into any agent, or ask in your own words. For a pending Plan, **Approve and copy** approves it and copies the request; after approval, **Ready to build** offers **Copy prompt**.

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Tip>Runs start in the agent's own [permission mode](../agents/native.mdx#permission-modes). Its own permission and sign-in prompts still need you, and a stop or pause stays in force.</Tip>

### Where the build lands {#where-it-lands}

A new branch or worktree starts at this checkout's HEAD. A worktree's name sets its branch and its folder beside the project; by command, `qualitylayer branch new [name]`. A pull request needs a branch other than its target. Pushes and deployments need the Plan's authorization; you merge.

## While the agent builds {#while-the-agent-builds}

![Slices built test first, one after another, then the checks in Verify](pathname:///img/diagrams/slices-light.svg)
![Slices built test first, one after another, then the checks in Verify](pathname:///img/diagrams/slices-dark.svg)

<Steps>
  <Step title="Slices">Your agent cuts the Plan into slices that each work end to end, thinnest first, and each slice into task cards. For a bug, the reproduction comes before the repair.</Step>
  <Step title="Test first">For each card it writes a failing test, builds the change and fixes failures. It may hand independent slices to subagents.</Step>
  <Step title="Done means">Test runs are recorded with their commit and exit code, so [Verify](verify.mdx) can cite them. Each **Done means** step runs on the built tree before Verify starts.</Step>
</Steps>

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="The board" icon="list-todo">Switch between **Board** and **Stack graph** in the Slices heading to follow parallel waves and dependencies; zoom, pan or open the map full size, or press **View diff** on a finished slice.</Card>
  <Card title="Under the board" icon="file-text">**Known limits**, **Decided while building** and **Program design**. A decision says whether it is build order or an amendment to what you approved.</Card>
  <Card title="Your part" icon="message-square">A matter only you can settle comes as one question; the build goes on while you answer.</Card>
</CardGroup>

<Note>A failing check is your agent's to fix, so the page does not flag it, and the final approval still refuses a red check. A login, secret or other prerequisite only you can provide never counts as passed. If it is still missing at the end of [Verify's checks](verify.mdx#when-it-stops), it reaches you as one question; the App never takes the secret.</Note>

## When the build is done {#when-done}

The session decides when the build is ready for its commit step. Verify starts on the committed revision. The default is a commit after each checked slice. In [Git and editor](../reference/settings.mdx#git-and-editor), you can choose one commit before Verify or review the checked worktree diff first. In that review, you can request edits, commit manually or approve the commit. Changed files need fresh checks and a fresh decision. Push has its own approval. Unticked cards and open needs stay open in Verify.

  { title: "Verify", href: "/docs/steps/verify", text: "Checks and a review by another agent, then yours." },
  { title: "Plan", href: "/docs/steps/plan", text: "What your agent asks and what you approve." },
  { title: "Supported agents", href: "/docs/agents/native", text: "Models and permissions per agent." },
]} />

title: Pull request
description: Open a GitHub pull request or copy a review draft for another repository host.

  format: mdx
---

import { Card, CardGroup, Steps, Step, Note, Screenshot, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

On [Verify](verify.mdx#approve), **Pull request** opens the prefilled pull request page after pushing the branch to GitHub.com. Create the request there, then your agent follows its checks and comments.

For GitLab, Bitbucket, GitHub Enterprise and other hosts, the header opens an editable title and description. Push the branch you want reviewed, then copy and paste the draft on your host. **Open** opens the repository when it has a web address. A local repository offers **Copy draft**. These drafts leave approval in QualityLayer.

<Screenshot name="pull-request" alt="The merged pull request: its checks, its reviewers and the time from the first question to the approval" caption="An example task in a fictional project." />

## How Verify follows it {#following}

On GitHub.com, QualityLayer finds the pull request by its branch, and the button then shows **#N · open**, or **#N · update** once the code moved. While the App is open, Verify reads checks and reviewers through `gh`. Without it, the task stays open until a pull or fetch brings the merge into local Git, or you mark it merged.

## Your agent watches the checks {#watch}

Your agent runs `qualitylayer pr watch` until the checks pass:

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="The checks pass" icon="badge-check">It checks open review threads and reads new comments, and asks you before changing anything they request.</Card>
  <Card title="A check fails" icon="triangle-alert">It reads the log, fixes the cause, pushes and watches again. It never weakens or skips a check.</Card>
  <Card title="The branch conflicts" icon="git-pull-request">It merges or rebases the way your repository does, checks that no commit was lost, then pushes.</Card>
  <Card title="Three attempts used" icon="info">It reports what still fails and stops.</Card>
</CardGroup>

<Note>Your agent never force-pushes commits that are not its own.</Note>

## When something waits for you {#waits}

![Review threads and failing checks come back to you; you push the fix for review threads; you merge](pathname:///img/diagrams/pull-request-light.svg)
![Review threads and failing checks come back to you; you push the fix for review threads; you merge](pathname:///img/diagrams/pull-request-dark.svg)

Failing checks, review threads and conflicts appear in **Needs you** while the App is open. [Watch pull requests](../reference/settings.mdx#git-and-editor) can wake or resume your agent, also for new comments.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Ask your agent">"Using QL, review task retry-webhooks", with your task's name.</Step>
  <Step title="It fixes the routine requests">Test first, against the code and the approved Plan. Scope or design changes, and replies ready to post, come to you.</Step>
  <Step title="Push the fix">For review threads, the push is yours: press **Push the fix**. Your replies post on GitHub in your name.</Step>
</Steps>

## When you merge {#merged}

When you merge, the task moves to **Shipped** with what it cost. A squash or rebase merge is recognized too; while no pull request is open, **Mark as merged** covers any other case. Its documents stay in `docs/plans/`. Further work starts with **Start a follow-up**.

]} />

A failure is never marked passed. ## The checks {#lanes} Project commands and scans produce recorded results: Open **Check results and checkout** to see each command’s outcome, the checked revision and the current checkout. Complexity and duplication in the files your agent changed, fed back to it after each turn. Secrets, dependency advisories, GitHub workflows and risky code. An unavailable scan stays **not checked**. A point passes only with evidence: a check's output, a captured response, a screenshot or a file. Separate agents review the code and its behavior: A separate agent reviews the whole diff and checks the integrated change. In a split first round, helpers run groups of **Done means** steps and record their results. When the change crosses a trust boundary or edits agent controls. Your agent fixes critical and high findings first. Checks each finished design before you see it, unless you turn **Design review** off in [Settings](../reference/settings.mdx#workflow). A reviewer from another agent family checks risky changes [when enabled](../reference/settings.mdx#second-opinion), or on request. Findings are **Taken** or **Kept**. With **Independent review** off in [Settings](../reference/settings.mdx#independent-review), no fresh agent checks the change, and Verify shows it as **skipped**. ## Fix and recheck {#rounds} A review fails on a **Done means** point, a red check, a critical or high security finding, lost data, or a bug it reproduces in the changed lines. Your agent fixes it and commits, re-runs prior failing cases alongside the fix, and a fresh reviewer rechecks what failed and what the fix changed. Unchanged environment blockers are parked as an owner request instead of looping another round. Your agent continues while it can make progress within the approved scope. ## When the checks cannot finish {#when-it-stops} If a check needs access or a decision only you can provide, your agent asks for it. In the App, **Owner requests** shows each open decision or evidence request. Other checks can continue while a request is open. A failing point still needs recorded evidence to pass. When Git proves that task commits were replaced, Verify checks the working tree in a fresh review. When Verify offers **Choose review commit**, select the checkout and commit you want reviewed. A shared checkout asks you to include other tasks’ changes. The new review checks the whole candidate against the approved Plan. Earlier evidence stays with its original revision. ## Review the result {#items} While checks run, the progress bar counts the points proven. Open agent activity for recorded outcomes and any action the agent needs from you. **Read the record** opens `agents/03-verify.md` with findings, commands and every judged round. The request in one sentence, then a release-note line for each change users see. An ordered stack of slices with viewed progress and Done means links. Click any slice to open its files first. Named diagrams beside an interactive, wave-filtered **Slice flow** map with zoom, pan and full-size view, and each screen switched between **Designed**, **Built**, or **Compare** when both are images. Each point as it ran, with its picture or output, and whether it ran as a script or in a real agent session. Anything only you can check, such as your account or a device the agents cannot run, comes to you as a question. What turns up while you review, your agent fixes at once; **rechecking** shows over the part that changed. **Export** saves your Review as PDF, Markdown with pictures or a web page. `03-verify.md` is the pull request description; pictures stay local unless you share them. For changed [lasting artifacts](../artifacts.mdx#lasting), choose which pages to [fold in](../artifacts.mdx#fold-in). ## Read the code {#code} **Review the code** opens the file tree and a **Unified / Split** diff. Click any slice in the tree to focus on its files, use **Focus** to hide the tree for wide split diffs, switch to **Since R1** after fix rounds to read only what changed since an earlier round, or open **Slice flow** to jump between slices. **Viewed** and **Mark slice viewed** save your reading progress; **All viewed** and **Clear** apply to every file. ### Ask about any line {#line-comments} Select the lines you want to discuss. Write in the quick feedback field and send it to your agent with the file, revision and selected lines. Sending it never approves the change or allows a push. ### Findings from the agents {#findings} Security and second-opinion findings appear on their lines. Request a change, or record why a finding is not a problem; the reason becomes a [project lesson](../memory.mdx) for later reviews. ### Ask another reviewer {#another-reviewer} **Ask another reviewer** picks an installed agent that did not build the change. It reviews one file or all files, edits nothing and stops after 8 minutes. ## Approve {#approve} Approve the whole change in the page header, also when its agent has stopped. Your approval always saves, even when the code moved after the checks or a recheck is running. Approves the change and never pushes. The conversation stays open for merge, deploy and tweaks. On GitHub.com, pushes the task's branch and opens the prefilled pull request page using `gh`. On other hosts, opens an editable draft to copy into your review. ### After you approve {#after-approve} Ask your agent to merge, push, deploy or run end-to-end tests; each still needs your request. | Verify shows | What you do | | --- | --- | | **Not merged yet** | Merge as usual. Merged on the web? Pull the base branch. While no pull request is open, **Mark as merged** works too | | **1 change since your approval** | Your agent committed a tweak. Press **View the change**, then **Approve change** in the header. With an open pull request, your merge accepts it | | **Merged into main** | The task is in **Shipped**. New work starts with **Start a follow-up** | QualityLayer recognizes local merges, including squash and rebase, and pull requests it opened on GitHub. For work built directly on main, only that task's fixes count ([details](implement.mdx#where-it-lands)).

import { Card, CardGroup, Steps, Step, Tabs, Tab, Tip, Note, Flow, NextSteps } from "@site/src/components/kit";

Plan, Implement and Verify run in your agent's chat. You answer the questions and approve the Plan and the finished change there. Open the App only to read the documents or review the code.

<Flow
  label="You ask your agent in plain words; it plans, builds and verifies, and asks you in its own picker"
  nodes={[
    { icon: "message-square", label: "You ask", detail: "In plain words" },
    { icon: "network", label: "Plan", detail: "Questions in the agent's picker", tone: "plan" },
    { icon: "code-xml", label: "Implement", detail: "Slices, test first", tone: "implement" },
    { icon: "shield-check", label: "Verify", detail: "Your final approval", tone: "verify" },
  ]}
/>

## Start a task {#start}

Ask in plain words:

```text
Using QualityLayer, plan a CSV export.
```

If you ask your agent to plan without naming QualityLayer, it offers QualityLayer once and you pick **Yes** or **No**. An ordinary coding request never starts a workflow.

<Tip>To turn the offer off, clear **Offer QualityLayer** in [Settings › Workflow](reference/settings.mdx#workflow), or run `qualitylayer settings set offerWorkflow false`.</Tip>

## Choose where you answer and approve {#where}

Your first task started in your agent asks once, in the agent's own picker:

<CardGroup cols={3}>
  <Card title="Here in your agent" icon="square-terminal">Questions and approvals in its chat, such as **Here in Claude Code**.</Card>
  <Card title="In the App" icon="app-window">Questions and approvals in the App.</Card>
  <Card title="Questions here" icon="message-square">Questions in your agent, approvals in the App.</Card>
</CardGroup>

Your pick is saved and not asked again. Change it in **Settings › Workflow** (**Answer questions in** and **Approve in**), or by command (`app` sends it to the App, `terminal` keeps it in your agent):

```sh
qualitylayer settings set answers terminal
qualitylayer settings set approvals terminal
qualitylayer task set answers=terminal approvals=app   # this task only
```

The two rows also allow questions in the App with approvals in your agent.

<Note>Tasks you start in the App always answer in the App.</Note>

## What you see in your agent {#what-you-see}

<Steps>
  <Step title="Questions">In Plan, in the agent's own picker.</Step>
  <Step title="The Plan">A short summary and the path of the full file, any **Your call** to settle, then **Approve Plan**, **Give feedback** or **Show the Plan**.</Step>
  <Step title="Where to build">**Build here, from the Plan** (compact, then say "build here"), **Keep this conversation** or **Another session or agent**.</Step>
  <Step title="Verify">The final approval, once every point is proven.</Step>
</Steps>

Only your own pick or words count as an answer or an approval. The Plan in a fictional task:

```text
Plan ready: Add a CSV export to the Orders page
Adds an Export button that downloads the rows you filtered.
Full text: docs/plans/csv-export/01-plan.md

  Approve Plan
  Give feedback
  Show the Plan
```

## Agents and pickers {#pickers}

| Agent | How you answer |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode, Grok, Antigravity, GitHub Copilot | The agent's own picker |
| Cursor | Numbered choices in the chat. Type the number or your own words. |

Setup turns on Codex's question picker and lets Grok's questions wait for you instead of expiring. If you turned the picker off in Codex, it uses numbered choices. `qualitylayer doctor` shows whether each installed agent's picker is ready.

## Use the App anyway {#app}

You can answer the same open question directly in the App. The agent stays your preferred place for the next question. The App names the native picker when it has seen the question there.

QualityLayer
The software factory with you in the loop

**Plan, implement and verify software with your favorite coding agents.**
Work side by side in the App or browser, or in your own agent: terminal, IDE or agent app.

Install • Workflow • Docs • Website • Changelog • Issues

Download the App  

  Watch the [full-resolution video](https://qualitylayer-media.max-ritter.workers.dev/hero-walkthrough-v2026111301.mp4) or [try the demo](https://qualitylayer.dev/app-demo/?story&guide) in your browser. Fictional project.
--- ## Why QualityLayer > “With QualityLayer, developing software with agents finally feels like doing real engineering again.” > > *An engineer who uses QualityLayer* | You get | How it works | | --- | --- | | **Your own agent and plan** | Use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more with your existing login or API key. | | **A design you can review** | Ask your agent about diagrams and clickable screens, then approve the Plan before code changes. | | **Small, tested changes** | Your agent writes tests before code and hands independent parts to other agents when useful. | | **An independent check** | With independent review on, a separate agent checks the running change against your request before you review it. | | **Your own requirements** | Add checks, tools or skills to any step. Your agent records what ran, what did not, and why. [Step checks](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/reference/settings#step-checks). | | **Your own automations** | Send task events to a URL or a command, and read or start tasks from a script. [Automations](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/automations). | | **Visible decisions and effort** | Read decisions and results in your repository; see time, model usage value and cost estimates in the App. | ---

Getting started

### Prerequisites - **A coding agent**, installed and signed in with your subscription or API key: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Antigravity, Pi, OpenCode or GitHub Copilot. [Other agents](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/agents/other) connect through the CLI. - **Git** and a repository. ### Installation **[Download the App](https://qualitylayer.dev/download)** and open it. Setup automatically installs the `qualitylayer` command ([commands](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/reference/commands)) and connects your agents. On a server, in WSL or in a container: ```bash curl -fsSL https://qualitylayer.dev/install.sh | bash # macOS, Linux, WSL irm https://qualitylayer.dev/install.ps1 | iex # Windows PowerShell ``` The App updates itself; without it, run `qualitylayer update`. To work on a Linux or macOS machine you reach over ssh, add it under **Settings › Machines**: the App installs QualityLayer there and lets you set up its agents and projects. [Installation guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/install).
Uninstalling `qualitylayer uninstall` undoes what the installer changed; your plans stay. On Windows, even when the App is gone: ```powershell & ([scriptblock]::Create((irm https://qualitylayer.dev/install.ps1))) -Uninstall ```
Coming from Pilot Shell 11 Run `pilot update` or download the App. An active Pilot Shell licence works with both products; older purchases may need help moving over. [Migration and memory import](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/moving-from-pilot-shell).
### First steps In the App or browser, choose **+**, then **Task** (Feature or Bugfix) or **Chat**. Pick your repository and agent, and describe what you need: ```text Plan retries for failed webhooks and stop after a few tries. ``` 1. Answer questions and ask your agent to revise the Plan. 2. Approve the Plan. Your agent builds and verifies the change. 3. Review the result and recorded checks, then approve it. Ask your agent to merge, deploy or make further changes. Prefer your terminal, IDE or agent app? Choose **In my own agent**, or ask there: “Using QualityLayer, plan retries for failed webhooks.” Other agents use the CLI ([supported agents](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/agents/native)). **Chat** skips the workflow steps ([Chat guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/chat)). QualityLayer runs only when you ask for it. [Your first task](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/first-task). ### Skills your agent gets Setup adds these skills. Ask in plain words, in any language. | Skill | For | You say | | --- | --- | --- | | `ql-peer` | Agents talking to each other | “Ask Codex to review what you just built.” | | `ql-workflow` | Plan, implement and verify a change | “Using QualityLayer, add rate limits to the export API.” | | `ql-chat` | Chat without workflow steps | “Using QualityLayer, chat about the billing refactor.” | | `ql-artifact` | Designs, diagrams and pages | “Open the settings design in my browser.” | | `ql-quality` | Code health and security scans | “Scan this repository for leaked secrets.” | | `ql-manage` | Tasks, settings and setup | “Show my open tasks.” | [More about the skills](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/agents/native#the-six-skills) ---

The workflow

Three steps, two approvals. You plan and you verify; agents do everything between. Each step is one page in the App and one Markdown file in your repository, and existing plans start at Plan. ### 1 · Plan, approved by you Your agent reads the code, asks what only you can answer and writes one Plan: **Done means**, named diagrams and clickable screens. Compare revisions after feedback. Bugs are reproduced and diagnosed here. [Plan guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/steps/plan) ### 2 · Implement, by your agents Your agent cuts the Plan into slices and task cards, writes a failing test before each change and hands independent slices to other agents. Follow progress on the slice board or dependency graph, and open any finished slice's diff. By default it commits after each checked slice; you can choose one commit before Verify or review the checked worktree diff first. [Implement guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/steps/implement) ### 3 · Verify, then approved by you Agents that did not write the code check every point and fix what fails. Then the same page is your review: an ordered stack of slices, a slice dependency graph, built screens and each point as it ran. [Verify guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/steps/verify) **Then the pull request.** Your agent fixes failing checks and routine review threads; the task stays open until you merge. [Pull request guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/steps/pull-request) ## Checks and independent review Your project's checks, [code health](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/reference/code-health) and security scans run first. Then a separate agent reviews the change against your request. [How Verify works](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/steps/verify). ## QualityLayer App | In the App | What you can do | | --- | --- | | **Chat or a planned task** | Talk directly with your agent or follow the workflow. See agent activity and get notified when one needs you. | | **Conversation and terminal** | Read the agent's conversation or its terminal beside the task. Answer questions and send quick feedback on marked text, code or artifact spots. | | **Artifacts** | Try clickable designs, keep them in your repository, and export designs, Plans and Reviews for teammates. [Artifacts guide](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/artifacts). | | **Checks and code review** | Read the evidence, review diffs slice by slice or since the last check round, and ask your agent about any line. | | **Agent controls and usage** | Switch agents, choose model, effort and permissions; track limits and daily costs, including in the macOS menu bar. [Settings](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/reference/settings). | | **Local memory** | Reuse [project lessons](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/memory), with optional project Git export and explicit repository import. | QualityLayer keeps tasks, Chats, artifacts and memories on machines you control. Your coding agent uses its own provider. [Files and privacy](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/reference/files#privacy). [Read about the App](https://qualitylayer.dev/docs/app) ---
**Quality by design.** The software factory with you in the loop. Made by [Max Ritter](https://maxritter.net) · [License](LICENSE)
